events.title: Battle of Henan-Hunan-Guangxi
events.short: In 1944 Japan's Henan-Hunan-Guangxi campaign sought a continental rail and road link; Kuomintang forces collapsed, losing much of Henan, Hunan, Guangxi and Guangdong in eight months.
events.detail: In 1944 Japan was losing ground in the Pacific, and its sea lanes were under serious threat from US forces. To open a land route from northeast China to Vietnam, the Japanese army massed over 500,000 troops for a major attack on the Kuomintang front, known as Operation Ichi-Go and in China as the Battle of Henan-Hunan-Guangxi. In April 1944 the Japanese struck Henan first; 400,000 Kuomintang troops under Tang Enbo and others collapsed at the first blow and in little more than a month lost 38 cities including Zhengzhou and Luoyang. In May the Japanese attacked Hunan and took Changsha in June. They then besieged Hengyang, where Fang Xianjue, commander of the 10th Army, held out for 47 days and inflicted heavy casualties, falling at last for lack of relief and ammunition. In September the Japanese attacked Guangxi, took Guilin and Liuzhou in November, and in early December a detachment reached Dushan in Guizhou, alarming Chongqing. In eight months the Kuomintang lost 500,000 to 600,000 men and large areas of Henan, Hunan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian and Guizhou, along with 146 cities, leaving over 60 million Chinese under Japanese rule. The great rout exposed the corruption of Kuomintang rule and the weakness of its army, and people in Kuomintang areas strongly demanded an end to one-party dictatorship and a democratic coalition government. Meanwhile the battlefield behind enemy lines under the Communist Party began partial counteroffensives from 1944, recovering large areas and expanding the liberated areas. In spring 1945 Chinese forces defeated the Japanese in the Battle of West Hunan, and the situation on the main front improved somewhat.

events.title: Seventh National Congress of the CCP
events.short: Meeting in Yan'an from April to June 1945, the CCP's Seventh National Congress made Mao Zedong Thought its guide and set the goal of defeating Japan and building a new China.
events.detail: In 1945, with final victory in the War of Resistance approaching, China faced a choice between two futures, bright or dark. From 23 April to 11 June 1945 the Chinese Communist Party held its Seventh National Congress at Yangjialing in Yan'an, attended by over 700 delegates and alternate delegates representing more than 1.2 million Party members. Mao Zedong gave the political report On Coalition Government, Zhu De the military report On the Battlefields of the Liberated Areas, and Liu Shaoqi the report on revising the Party constitution. The congress summed up the twists and turns of more than twenty years of the Party's leadership of the democratic revolution and set the political line of "boldly mobilizing the masses and expanding the people's forces, so that under the Party's leadership we defeat the Japanese aggressors, liberate the whole people and build a New Democratic China." It adopted a new Party constitution establishing Mao Zedong Thought as the Party's guiding ideology and writing it into the constitution. It summed up the three fine styles of work formed in the Party's long revolutionary struggle: integrating theory with practice, maintaining close ties with the masses, and practicing self-criticism. It elected a new Central Committee headed by Mao Zedong. Called the "Congress of Unity and Victory," it laid the political, ideological and organizational foundation for final victory in the War of Resistance and for the nationwide victory of the New Democratic Revolution. The congress site at Yangjialing, Yan'an, is now a major national cultural heritage site.

events.title: Victory in the War of Resistance Against Japan
events.short: Japan announced unconditional surrender on 15 August 1945 and signed the instrument of surrender on 2 September, ending the war of resistance in victory; Taiwan was returned to China.
events.detail: From 1944 to early 1945, news from the world anti-fascist front was a stream of victories, and Germany's defeat in Europe was assured. Germany surrendered unconditionally in May 1945. On 26 July China, the United States and Britain issued the Potsdam Proclamation urging Japan's unconditional surrender and reaffirming that the Cairo Declaration must be carried out, requiring Japan to return the Chinese territories it had stolen, including the Northeast, Taiwan and the Penghu Islands. On 6 and 9 August the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. On 8 August the Soviet Union declared war on Japan and sent troops into northeast China. Under heavy blows from the Chinese people and anti-fascist forces worldwide, the Japanese emperor announced unconditional surrender on 15 August 1945. On 2 September Japanese representatives signed the instrument of surrender aboard the US battleship Missouri in Tokyo Bay. On 9 September the surrender ceremony for the China Theater was held in Nanjing, where Okamura Yasuji, commander-in-chief of Japanese forces in China, handed the instrument of surrender to He Yingqin, commander-in-chief of the Chinese Army. On 25 October the ceremony for Taiwan was held in Taipei, and Taiwan and the Penghu Islands, occupied by Japan for fifty years, returned to China. The Chinese people's War of Resistance was the first war of national liberation in modern times in which China completely defeated a foreign invader, and the Chinese theater was the main Eastern theater of the world anti-fascist war. In fourteen years of resistance, Chinese military and civilian casualties exceeded 35 million, an enormous national sacrifice. After the victory, China became a founding member of the United Nations and one of the permanent members of the Security Council. In 2014 the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress designated 3 September as Victory Day of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japan.

events.title: Chongqing Negotiations and the Double Tenth Agreement
events.short: In August 1945 Mao Zedong went to Chongqing at Chiang Kai-shek's invitation; on 10 October they signed the Double Tenth Agreement, with the Kuomintang accepting peaceful reconstruction.
events.detail: After victory in the War of Resistance, China faced the question of what kind of state to build. Chiang Kai-shek sought to establish one-party Kuomintang rule, but his civil-war preparations were incomplete, the main Kuomintang forces were still far away in the southwest and northwest, and opinion at home and abroad demanded peace, so he telegraphed Mao Zedong three times to come to Chongqing "to discuss national affairs together." One of his aims was to buy time to start a civil war. To seek peace, the Communist Party decided to send Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Wang Ruofei to the talks. On 28 August 1945 Mao flew from Yan'an to Chongqing accompanied by US Ambassador Patrick Hurley and Kuomintang representative Zhang Zhizhong. His going in person showed the Party's sincerity in seeking peace. In Chongqing Mao wrote out his poem Snow, to the tune of Qinyuanchun, as a gift to Liu Yazi, causing a sensation in the city. After forty-three days of arduous negotiations, on 10 October the two sides signed the Summary of Talks Between the Government and the Communist Party Representatives, known as the Double Tenth Agreement. The Kuomintang accepted the basic policy of peaceful national reconstruction, agreed to convene a Political Consultative Conference and recognized the equal legal status of all parties. But no agreement was reached on the governments of the liberated areas or on the people's army. To show its goodwill the Communist Party made concessions, voluntarily withdrawing from eight liberated areas including those in Guangdong and Zhejiang. In January 1946 the Political Consultative Conference met in Chongqing and adopted agreements including a program for peaceful national reconstruction, but the Kuomintang soon tore up both the Double Tenth Agreement and the conference resolutions. The sites of the negotiations survive at Hongyan Village and Guiyuan in Chongqing.

images.caption: Mao Zedong and Chiang Kai-shek photographed together during the Chongqing negotiations

events.title: Outbreak of Full-Scale Civil War
events.short: In June 1946 the Kuomintang attacked the Central Plains Liberated Area, starting full-scale civil war; the People's Liberation Army fought an active defense and broke the general offensive.
events.detail: After victory in the War of Resistance, Chiang Kai-shek, backed by the United States, actively prepared for civil war. In June 1946 he openly tore up the Double Tenth Agreement and the Political Consultative Conference resolutions and attacked the Central Plains Liberated Area with 300,000 troops, starting full-scale civil war. At the time the Kuomintang army numbered 4.3 million, with large quantities of US-supplied weapons, and controlled about three quarters of the country along with the big cities and main lines of communication; the People's Liberation Army had only a little over 1.2 million poorly equipped men, and the liberated areas were mainly in the countryside. Facing the Kuomintang offensive, the Communist Party led soldiers and civilians in the liberated areas in a war of self-defense. Forces of the Central Plains Liberated Area under Li Xiannian and others broke out successfully. Mao Zedong set a policy of active defense, "with the destruction of the enemy's effective strength as the main objective, not the holding or seizing of territory," concentrating superior forces to destroy the enemy piece by piece. In the Battle of Central Jiangsu, Su Yu led the Central China Field Army to seven victories in seven battles, destroying over 50,000 enemy troops. In a conversation with the American journalist Anna Louise Strong, Mao also put forward his famous statement that "all reactionaries are paper tigers." After eight months of fighting the Liberation Army had wiped out 710,000 Kuomintang troops and crushed the general offensive. Meanwhile the Communist Party carried out land reform in the liberated areas, issuing the May Fourth Directive in May 1946 and promulgating the Outline Land Law of China in October 1947 to give land to the tillers, and peasants joined the army and supported the front eagerly. In Kuomintang areas the people also launched a patriotic democratic movement against hunger, civil war and persecution, forming a second front.

images.caption: The United States airlifts Kuomintang troops to the civil war front in military aircraft

events.title: Crushing the Key-Point Offensive (Shaanbei and Menglianggu)
events.short: In 1947 the Kuomintang struck at northern Shaanxi and Shandong; Mao led the Central Committee through northern Shaanxi, and the East China Field Army destroyed the 74th Division at Menglianggu.
events.detail: In March 1947, after the general offensive had been blunted, Kuomintang forces turned to key-point attacks on the Shaanbei and Shandong liberated areas. In northern Shaanxi, Hu Zongnan led over 200,000 men against Yan'an, while the Liberation Army there numbered only some 20,000. To preserve its strength, Mao Zedong decided to evacuate Yan'an voluntarily, saying: "If we keep the men and lose the land, both men and land will be kept; if we keep the land and lose the men, both men and land will be lost." Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Ren Bishi led the Party Central Committee organs in remaining in northern Shaanxi to direct the national war of liberation, while Liu Shaoqi, Zhu De and others formed the Central Working Committee and went to North China. Peng Dehuai and Xi Zhongxun led the Northwest Field Army in "dawdling" tactics, wearing the enemy down, and won three battles in a row at Qinghuabian, Yangmaghe and Panlong, destroying over 14,000 enemy troops and stabilizing the situation in northern Shaanxi. In Shandong, the Kuomintang massed 450,000 troops against the liberated area. In May 1947 the East China Field Army under Chen Yi and Su Yu concentrated superior forces and wiped out the entire reorganized 74th Division, over 32,000 men, in the Menglianggu area of Mengyin County, Shandong, killing its commander Zhang Lingfu. The battle crushed the Kuomintang's key-point offensive in Shandong. The people of the Yimeng mountain area gave eager support to the front, and moving stories emerged such as that of the "Red Sisters of Yimeng," who nursed the wounded with their own milk. By June 1947, after a year of fighting, the Liberation Army had destroyed 1.12 million Kuomintang troops, the key-point offensive had been crushed, and the course of the war had turned in the Liberation Army's favor. The Liberation Army then moved to a strategic offensive.

events.title: Liu-Deng Army Leaps to the Dabie Mountains
events.short: In summer 1947 Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping led their field army across the Yellow River and a thousand li south into the Dabie Mountains, opening the Liberation Army's strategic offensive.
events.detail: After a year of fighting on interior lines, the Liberation Army had crushed the Kuomintang's general and key-point offensives, and the course of the war had turned in the people's favor. To carry the war into Kuomintang territory, on the night of 30 June 1947 Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping led over 120,000 men of the main force of the Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Field Army across the Yellow River in southwestern Shandong, and won the Battle of Southwest Shandong. The army then marched without a rear base straight into the heart of Kuomintang territory, reaching the Dabie Mountains at the end of August. The Dabie Mountains lie where Hubei, Henan and Anhui meet, pressing on Nanjing to the east and Wuhan to the west and bordering the Yangtze to the south, a position of great strategic importance. After entering the mountains the Liu-Deng army quickly deployed, set up base areas, and with local support crushed Kuomintang encirclement attacks and gained a firm footing. At the same time the Taiyue Column under Chen Geng and Xie Fuzhi advanced into western Henan, and the main force of the East China Field Army under Chen Yi and Su Yu advanced into the Henan-Anhui-Jiangsu border region. The three armies formed a triangular formation between the Yangtze, Huai, Yellow and Han Rivers, cooperating and fighting in mobile warfare, and created the Central Plains Liberated Area. On other fronts the Liberation Army likewise went over to the offensive. The leap into the Dabie Mountains opened the strategic offensive, carried the war into Kuomintang territory, and made the Central Plains the forward base for attacking Nanjing and Wuhan, the centers of Kuomintang rule. In December 1947 Mao Zedong declared: "The Chinese people's revolutionary war has now reached a turning point."

sources.title: Wikipedia (Chinese) - Advance into the Dabie Mountains

events.title: Outline Land Law of China and Land Reform
events.short: The 1947 Outline Land Law of China abolished feudal land exploitation and gave land to the tillers; peasants in the liberated areas received land and rallied to support the army.
events.detail: During the War of Resistance, to unite the landlord class against Japan, the Communist Party applied a policy of reduced rents and interest in the base areas. After victory, peasants urgently wanted land. The Party adjusted its land policy in time: on 4 May 1946 the Central Committee issued the Directive on the Land Question, known as the May Fourth Directive, which changed the policy from reducing rents and interest to confiscating landlords' land and distributing it to peasants, so that land would belong to those who tilled it. From July to September 1947 the Central Working Committee held the National Land Conference at Xibaipo in Pingshan County, Hebei, which drew up the Outline Land Law of China, promulgated by the Party Central Committee that October. The outline provided for abolishing the feudal and semi-feudal system of land exploitation and establishing land to the tiller; abolishing all landlords' land ownership; and having peasant associations take over all landlords' land and public land in the villages and, together with all other village land, distribute it equally according to the village's whole population, regardless of sex or age. After its promulgation a wave of land reform swept the liberated areas, and by autumn 1948 feudal exploitation had been eliminated in liberated areas of about 100 million people. Leftist deviations during the reform, such as infringing on middle peasants' interests and random beatings and killings, were later corrected. The success of land reform made peasants in the liberated areas masters of their own fate, led them to join the army and fight eagerly, and made the liberated areas a solid rear for victory. The outline was the guiding document for land reform in the war and laid a firm mass foundation for victory.

events.title: Regional Ethnic Autonomy (Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region)
events.short: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Government was founded in May 1947, China's first provincial-level ethnic autonomous area; regional ethnic autonomy later became a basic political system of the country.
events.detail: China is a unified multi-ethnic country. Based on the historical features and present conditions of its ethnic question, the Communist Party made regional ethnic autonomy its basic policy for resolving ethnic issues. After victory in the War of Resistance, under the Party's leadership, the people of Inner Mongolia carried out an autonomy movement. On 1 May 1947 the Inner Mongolia People's Congress met at Wangyemiao (now Ulanhot, Inner Mongolia) and announced the founding of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Government, with Ulanhu elected chairman; it was the first provincial-level ethnic minority autonomous area established under the Party's leadership. In September 1949 the Common Program adopted by the first plenary session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference provided that regional autonomy should be practiced in areas where minorities live in concentrated communities. In 1954 the system of regional ethnic autonomy was written into the Constitution of the People's Republic of China. The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (1955), the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region (1958, with the Zhuang name written in its current form from 1965), the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region (1958) and the Tibet Autonomous Region (1965) followed. Today China has five autonomous regions, 30 autonomous prefectures and over a hundred autonomous counties (banners). Together with the people's congress system, the system of multiparty cooperation and political consultation led by the Communist Party, and the system of grassroots self-government, regional ethnic autonomy forms the country's basic political system. It safeguards the right of ethnic minorities to be their own masters.

images.caption: Diagram of regional ethnic autonomy

events.title: Liaoshen Campaign
events.short: In the Liaoshen Campaign of September–November 1948, the Northeast Field Army took Jinzhou first to cut off retreat, destroyed over 470,000 enemy troops and liberated the whole Northeast.
events.detail: After two years of fighting, by autumn 1948 the Liberation Army had grown to 2.8 million men while the Kuomintang army had fallen to 3.65 million. The Party Central Committee judged the time ripe for decisive strategic battles and launched in turn the Liaoshen, Huaihai and Pingjin Campaigns. The Northeast was where the decisive battles began. There, 550,000 Kuomintang troops were split and confined in three isolated areas, Changchun, Shenyang and Jinzhou, and were considering withdrawing south of the Great Wall. On 12 September 1948 Lin Biao and Luo Ronghuan led the Northeast Field Army in launching the Liaoshen Campaign. Mao Zedong decided to strike Jinzhou first, "shutting the door to catch the dog," to seal the Kuomintang forces in the Northeast and destroy them where they stood. After fierce fighting the Northeast Field Army took Jinzhou on 15 October, wiping out its garrison of over 100,000 and capturing Fan Hanjie, deputy commander of the Kuomintang Northeast Bandit-Suppression headquarters, which cut the land route of withdrawal into China proper. At Tashan, the Northeast Field Army held off Kuomintang reinforcements advancing on Jinzhou from the direction of Huludao, securing victory at Jinzhou. After Jinzhou fell, part of the Changchun garrison rose in revolt and the rest surrendered, and Changchun was peacefully liberated. The army then surrounded and destroyed Liao Yaoxiang's army group in the Heishan and Dahushan area as it advanced west from Shenyang to try to retake Jinzhou. On 2 November the army took Shenyang and Yingkou, ending the campaign. The Liaoshen Campaign lasted 52 days, destroyed over 470,000 Kuomintang troops and liberated the entire Northeast. After it the Liberation Army for the first time outnumbered the Kuomintang army. The Liaoshen Campaign Memorial Hall stands in Jinzhou, Liaoning.

images.caption: Diagram of the three great campaigns

events.title: Huaihai Campaign
events.short: In late 1948 the Central Plains and East China Field Armies fought the Huaihai Campaign, destroying over 550,000 enemy troops and liberating most of East China and the Central Plains.
events.detail: After victory in the Liaoshen Campaign, the Party Central Committee decided to launch the Huaihai Campaign over the broad region centered on Xuzhou. For unified command it formed a General Front Committee of Liu Bocheng, Chen Yi, Deng Xiaoping, Su Yu and Tan Zhenlin, with Deng Xiaoping as secretary. On 6 November 1948 the Central Plains and East China Field Armies, 600,000 men in all, began the campaign against 800,000 Kuomintang troops. It had three stages. In the first, the East China Field Army destroyed Huang Baitao's army group at Nianzhuang, and Huang killed himself; He Jifeng and Zhang Kexia, deputy commanders of the Kuomintang Third Pacification Zone, led their troops in revolt. In the second, the Central Plains Field Army, with the East China Field Army, destroyed Huang Wei's army group in the Shuangduiji area of Su County, Anhui, and captured Huang Wei. In the third, the East China Field Army destroyed Du Yuming's group, which had withdrawn from Xuzhou, in the Chenguanzhuang area of Yongcheng, Henan, capturing Du Yuming and killing Qiu Qingquan. The campaign ended in victory on 10 January 1949 after 66 days, with the Liberation Army's 600,000 defeating 800,000 Kuomintang troops and destroying over 555,000 of them. East China and the Central Plains north of the Yangtze were largely liberated, and the Kuomintang capital Nanjing came under direct threat. It was the campaign that destroyed the most enemy troops and had the greatest political impact of the three. In it, over five million peasant laborers from East China, the Central Plains and other liberated areas supported the front, and Chen Yi said with deep feeling: "The victory of the Huaihai Campaign was pushed forward by the people on wheelbarrows." The Huaihai Campaign Martyrs' Memorial Tower and museum stand in Xuzhou, Jiangsu.

events.title: Pingjin Campaign and Peaceful Liberation of Beiping
events.short: In late 1948 the Northeast Field Army and North China forces launched the Pingjin Campaign, taking Tianjin and peacefully liberating Beiping, destroying or reorganizing over 520,000 Kuomintang troops.
events.detail: Almost at the same time as the Huaihai Campaign, the Northeast Field Army entered the Great Wall passes and, with the North China People's Liberation Army, launched the Pingjin Campaign. At the time over 500,000 troops under Fu Zuoyi, commander of the Kuomintang North China Bandit-Suppression headquarters, were spread along the line of Beiping, Tianjin, Zhangjiakou and Tanggu, intending to hold on or withdraw south by sea. The campaign began on 29 November 1948. The Liberation Army followed a policy of "isolating without surrounding" and "surrounding without attacking," first encircling Zhangjiakou and Xinbao'an. In late December it took Xinbao'an and Zhangjiakou, destroying Fu Zuoyi's main force of loyal troops. On 14 January 1949 the Liberation Army launched a general assault on the Tianjin garrison, which had refused to surrender, and after 29 hours of fierce fighting took the city, wiping out over 130,000 defenders and capturing Chen Changjie, the Tianjin garrison commander. With Tianjin liberated, the 200,000-plus garrison in Beiping was in an impossible position and Fu Zuoyi accepted terms of peaceful reorganization. On 31 January the Liberation Army entered Beiping, which was peacefully liberated. The peaceful liberation spared the historic and cultural city from the ravages of war and created the "Beiping model" of peacefully resolving the problem of remaining Kuomintang forces. The Pingjin Campaign lasted 64 days and destroyed or reorganized over 520,000 Kuomintang troops, largely liberating North China. The three campaigns together lasted 142 days and destroyed or reorganized over 1.54 million Kuomintang troops, essentially wiping out the main military force on which the Kuomintang's rule depended and greatly hastening nationwide victory. The Pingjin Campaign Memorial Hall stands in Tianjin.

images.caption: Diagram of the three great campaigns

events.title: Second Plenary Session of the Seventh CCP Central Committee
events.short: The Second Plenary Session of the Seventh Central Committee met at Xibaipo in March 1949, shifting the Party's focus from the countryside to the cities, and Mao Zedong set out the "Two Musts."
events.detail: After the three great campaigns, nationwide liberation was a foregone conclusion. To meet the final victory of the people's war and prepare for the founding of a new China, the Party Central Committee held the Second Plenary Session of the Seventh Central Committee at Xibaipo in Pingshan County, Hebei, from 5 to 13 March 1949. Mao Zedong gave an important report, and the session set the basic policies the Party should adopt in politics, economics and foreign affairs after nationwide victory. It decided that the focus of the Party's work would shift from the countryside to the cities, and that urban work must center on production and construction. The session also put forward foreign policy principles such as "starting anew" and "cleaning the house before inviting guests." In his report Mao warned the whole Party: "Winning nationwide victory is only the first step in a long march of ten thousand li." He asked that "comrades must be made to keep on being modest, prudent and free from arrogance and rashness in their work style, and to keep on with the style of plain living and hard struggle," the "Two Musts." To guard against a personality cult, on Mao's proposal the session also resolved to forbid celebrating the birthdays of Party leaders and to forbid naming places, streets and enterprises after them. On 23 March the Central Committee left Xibaipo for Beiping. Mao called the trip "going to the capital to take the examination" and said, "We must not be like Li Zicheng." The plenary session prepared the founding of New China politically and ideologically, and the "Two Musts" became a fine tradition of the Communist Party.

sources.title: Wikipedia (Chinese) - Second Plenary Session of the 7th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party

events.title: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign and Liberation of Nanjing
events.short: On 21 April 1949 a million Liberation Army troops crossed the Yangtze, and on 23 April they took Nanjing, marking the collapse of Kuomintang rule on the mainland.
events.detail: After the three great campaigns the Kuomintang's main military force had largely been destroyed. To gain time and rebuild its army, Chiang Kai-shek announced his "retirement" in January 1949, and Vice President Li Zongren became acting president and entered peace talks with the Communist Party, hoping to "divide China at the Yangtze." In April 1949 delegates of both sides held talks in Beiping, but the Nanjing National Government refused to sign the peace agreement and the talks broke down. On 21 April Mao Zedong and Zhu De issued the Order to the Army for a Nationwide Advance. One million men of the Second and Third Field Armies, along a front of over 500 kilometers from Hukou in Jiangxi in the west to Jiangyin in Jiangsu in the east, crossed the Yangtze in three columns and quickly broke through the river defenses the Kuomintang had labored to build. The Kuomintang Navy's Second Coastal Defense Fleet rose in revolt near Nanjing. On 23 April the Liberation Army occupied Nanjing, the center of Kuomintang rule, and the Kuomintang government moved to Guangzhou, marking the collapse of its rule on the mainland. On hearing the news, Mao wrote the famous lines "Wind and rain sweep over Zhongshan Mountain, a million brave troops cross the great river," and "We should pursue the retreating enemy with all our remaining strength, and not seek vain fame like the overlord of Chu." The Liberation Army then pressed on, liberating Hangzhou, Wuhan and Shanghai in May, while the Fourth and First Field Armies advanced into Central-South and Northwest China; by 1950 the whole mainland except for Taiwan and some islands was largely liberated. The Memorial Hall of the Yangtze Crossing Victory in Nanjing, Jiangsu, presents this history.

images.caption: Liberation Army troops force the Yangtze crossing

events.title: First Plenary Session of the CPPCC
events.short: In September 1949 the first plenary session of the CPPCC adopted the Common Program as an interim constitution, elected the Central People's Government and chose the flag, anthem and capital.
events.detail: On 30 April 1948 the Party Central Committee issued its May Day slogans, calling on the democratic parties, people's organizations and public figures to convene a political consultative conference quickly and form a democratic coalition government, which drew an enthusiastic response. A large number of democrats then broke through the Kuomintang blockade and reached the liberated areas in succession to discuss the founding of the state. In June 1949 the preparatory committee for the new Political Consultative Conference met in Beiping. From 21 to 30 September 1949 the First Plenary Session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference was held in grand fashion in Beiping, attended by over 600 delegates from all sectors. The session exercised the powers of the National People's Congress and adopted the Common Program of the CPPCC, which served as a provisional constitution and provided that New China would practice a people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class, based on the alliance of workers and peasants, and uniting all democratic classes and all ethnic groups. It also adopted the Organic Law of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China and elected Mao Zedong chairman of the Central People's Government, with Zhu De, Liu Shaoqi, Soong Ching-ling, Li Jishen, Zhang Lan and Gao Gang as vice chairmen. The session decided that the capital of the People's Republic of China would be Beiping, renamed Beijing; that the Five-Star Red Flag would be the national flag; that until a national anthem was formally adopted, March of the Volunteers would serve as the anthem; and that the Common Era calendar would be used. It also decided to build the Monument to the People's Heroes in Tiananmen Square, and all delegates laid its foundation stone. The session marked the formal establishment of the system of multiparty cooperation and political consultation under Communist Party leadership and made full preparations for the birth of New China.

events.title: Founding of the People's Republic of China
events.short: On 1 October 1949, before 300,000 soldiers and civilians in Tiananmen Square, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China.
events.detail: On the afternoon of 1 October 1949 the Central People's Government Council held its first plenary meeting at Zhongnanhai, appointing Zhou Enlai premier of the Government Administration Council and foreign minister, Mao Zedong chairman of the People's Revolutionary Military Commission, and Zhu De commander-in-chief of the People's Liberation Army. At 3 p.m., 300,000 soldiers and civilians gathered in Tiananmen Square in Beijing for the grand founding ceremony. Chairman Mao Zedong solemnly proclaimed from the Tiananmen gate tower: "The Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China is established today!" and pressed the button himself to raise the first Five-Star Red Flag. Fifty-four cannons then fired a 28-gun salute, symbolizing the 28 years of struggle of the Chinese people under the Communist Party. A grand military parade followed, in which Commander-in-Chief Zhu De reviewed the naval, ground and air forces and read the Order of the Headquarters of the Chinese People's Liberation Army. After the parade the crowds marched, and the celebrations continued into the night. The founding of the People's Republic was an epoch-making event in Chinese history. It ended more than a hundred years of humiliation by invasion and enslavement, making China a truly independent country; from then on, the Chinese people stood up and became masters of their country; and it ended long division and achieved a high degree of national unity and unprecedented ethnic solidarity. After the founding, the Soviet Union and other countries successively recognized the People's Republic and established diplomatic relations with it. In December the Central People's Government decided to make 1 October the National Day each year.

events.title: Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance
events.short: After Mao Zedong's visit to Moscow, China and the USSR signed a Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance in February 1950, as New China chose to "lean to one side."
events.detail: After its founding, New China followed an independent foreign policy of peace. At the founding ceremony Mao Zedong declared that the government was willing to establish diplomatic relations with any foreign government that observed principles of equality, mutual benefit and mutual respect for territorial sovereignty. In light of the international situation of the day, New China set three foreign policy principles: "starting anew," "cleaning the house before inviting guests," and "leaning to one side." On 2 October 1949 the Soviet Union was the first country to announce recognition of the People's Republic and establish relations. In the early period, newly independent Asian countries such as India, Indonesia and Burma, and Nordic countries such as Sweden, Denmark, Switzerland and Finland also established diplomatic relations with China, forming New China's first wave of diplomatic recognition. Mao Zedong visited the Soviet Union from December 1949 to February 1950. On 14 February 1950 Zhou Enlai and Soviet Foreign Minister Andrey Vyshinsky signed the Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance in Moscow. It provided that each side would give military aid if attacked by a third country, that the Soviet Union would grant China a loan of 300 million US dollars, and that it would return the Chinese Changchun Railway and Lushun (Port Arthur) and Dalian to China. The treaty replaced the 1945 Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance signed with the Nationalist government, upheld China's sovereignty and national dignity, aided economic recovery and national defense, and raised New China's international standing. The Soviet Union later helped China build 156 key projects, which played an important part in China's industrialization.

events.title: War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
events.short: In October 1950 the Chinese People's Volunteers entered the Korean War against the "UN forces"; an armistice was signed in July 1953.
events.detail: The Korean civil war broke out on 25 June 1950. The US government decided to intervene militarily and sent the Seventh Fleet into the Taiwan Strait. The United States then maneuvered the UN Security Council into passing resolutions that formed "UN forces" made up mainly of US troops, which crossed the 38th Parallel and advanced toward the Yalu River on the China-Korea border, bombing China's northeastern border areas. At the request of the Korean government, the Party Central Committee made the strategic decision to "resist US aggression, aid Korea, and defend the homeland." On 19 October 1950 the Chinese People's Volunteers, with Peng Dehuai as commander and political commissar, crossed the Yalu River into Korea and fought their first battle on 25 October. Fighting alongside the Korean People's Army, they drove the "UN forces" from the Yalu back to the vicinity of the 38th Parallel in five campaigns, after which the war entered a phase of fighting while negotiating. In 1952 the Volunteers held out stubbornly at Shangganling and crushed the "UN forces'" attacks. Many heroes emerged among them: Huang Jiguang blocked an enemy machine-gun port with his chest; Qiu Shaoyun died in flames rather than reveal his position; Yang Gensi clutched an explosive pack and died together with the enemy; and Mao Zedong's son Mao Anying also died on the Korean battlefield. On 27 July 1953 the two sides signed the Korean Armistice Agreement at Panmunjom. The victory protected China's security, won New China a relatively stable and peaceful environment for development, and greatly raised its international standing. In the war over 190,000 Volunteers gave their lives.

events.title: Land Reform in New China
events.short: The Land Reform Law of 1950 set out to end the feudal land system; by the end of 1952 land reform was essentially complete across mainland China.
events.detail: When New China was founded, the newly liberated areas, with more than half the country's population, had not yet carried out land reform, and the peasants were still bound by the feudal land system. In old China, landlords and rich peasants, under 10 percent of the rural population, held 70 to 80 percent of the land, while poor peasants, hired hands and middle peasants, over 90 percent of the rural population, owned only 20 to 30 percent. To free rural productive forces and develop agriculture, in June 1950 the Central People's Government promulgated the Land Reform Law of the People's Republic of China, which abolished the landlord class's feudal exploitative land ownership and established peasant land ownership. The general line of land reform was to rely on poor peasants and hired hands, unite with middle peasants, neutralize rich peasants, and eliminate the feudal system of exploitation step by step and in a differentiated way, in order to develop agricultural production. From winter 1950 land reform was carried out in the new liberated areas in stages, confiscating landlords' land, draft animals, farm tools, surplus housing and grain and distributing them to landless and land-poor peasants. By the end of 1952, except for some ethnic minority areas, land reform was essentially complete on the mainland: about 300 million landless and land-poor peasants received about 700 million mu of land and other means of production, and were freed from paying landlords some 35 billion kilograms of grain in heavy rent each year. Land reform destroyed the feudal land system that had lasted over 2,000 years, eliminated the landlord class, made peasants true masters of their own fate, liberated rural productive forces, and sped the recovery of agriculture, creating conditions for industrialization and socialist construction.

images.caption: The Land Reform Law of the People's Republic of China is warmly welcomed by the peasants

events.title: Peaceful Liberation of Tibet
events.short: In May 1951 the Central People's Government and the Tibetan local government signed the Seventeen Point Agreement, peacefully liberating Tibet and unifying the mainland.
events.detail: Tibet has been part of China's territory since ancient times. On the eve of New China's founding, some upper-class figures in the Tibetan local government, backed by foreign forces, tried to split Tibet from China and staged the "expulsion of Han" incident. At the time of the founding ceremony in 1949 the 10th Panchen Erdeni, then at Kumbum Monastery in Qinghai, telegrammed Mao Zedong and Zhu De asking for early liberation of Tibet. To uphold national sovereignty and territorial integrity, the Central People's Government decided to liberate Tibet peacefully. In October 1950 the Liberation Army launched the Qamdo Campaign and liberated Qamdo, opening the door to peaceful liberation. The Tibetan local government then sent a delegation headed by Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme to negotiate in Beijing. On 23 May 1951 the Central People's Government and the Tibetan local government signed in Beijing the Agreement on Measures for the Peaceful Liberation of Tibet, known as the Seventeen Point Agreement. It provided that the Tibetan people would unite and drive imperialist aggressive forces out of Tibet and return to the big family of the motherland, the People's Republic of China; that under the unified leadership of the Central People's Government the Tibetan people would have the right of regional ethnic autonomy; that the Central Government would not alter the existing political system of Tibet; and that the religious beliefs and customs of the Tibetan people would be respected. In October the Liberation Army entered Lhasa. To support Tibet's development the Kang-Tibet (Sichuan-Tibet) and Qinghai-Tibet highways were built, both opening in 1954. The peaceful liberation of Tibet unified the mainland, strengthened ethnic unity and opened a new chapter in Tibet's history.

events.title: Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan Case
events.short: In 1952 Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan were sentenced to death for embezzlement, the first major anti-corruption case of New China, which spurred the Three-Anti and Five-Anti campaigns.
events.detail: In New China's early years, some Party cadres grew complacent in peacetime, and embezzlement, waste and bureaucratism appeared. At the end of 1951 the Party Central Committee launched the Three-Anti campaign against corruption, waste and bureaucratism; in early 1952 it began the Five-Anti campaign among private industrialists and merchants. Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan were both veteran cadres who had joined the revolution many years earlier and contributed to it, and they successively served as Party secretary of the Tianjin prefecture. Using their positions, they misappropriated state disaster relief grain and funds, special river-control funds, and relief funds for cadres' families, embezzling and squandering over 17.1 billion yuan of public money (in old currency, about 1.71 million in new currency). After the case was exposed, the Hebei Provincial Party Committee proposed the death penalty for both. When some pleaded for leniency because they were veteran revolutionaries who had served, Mao Zedong said: "It is precisely because their positions were high, their merits great and their influence large that we must resolve to execute them. Only by executing them can we save 20, 200, 2,000 or 20,000 cadres who have committed errors of varying degrees." On 10 February 1952 the Hebei Provincial People's Court held a public trial in Baoding and sentenced Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan to death, with immediate execution. It was the first major anti-corruption case of New China. It showed the Party's determination to oppose corruption and govern itself strictly, and strongly advanced the Three-Anti and Five-Anti campaigns, which largely ended in October 1952 and created conditions for planned economic construction.

events.title: First Five-Year Plan
events.short: China's First Five-Year Plan (1953–1957) concentrated on heavy industry; plants such as the First Automobile Works in Changchun laid the first foundations of industrialization.
events.detail: New China began construction on a very backward economic base. Mao Zedong once said: "What can we make now? We can make tables and chairs, teacups and teapots... but we cannot make a single car, airplane, tank or tractor." After three years of economic recovery, the national economy was fully restored by the end of 1952. To change China's industrial backwardness and turn a backward agrarian country into an advanced industrial one, China began its first Five-Year Plan for the national economy in 1953. Its basic task was to concentrate main forces on industrial construction centered on 156 projects designed with Soviet help, within a total of 694 large and medium-sized projects, and to lay a preliminary foundation for socialist industrialization. Through the efforts of the whole people, by the end of 1957 most targets of the plan had been exceeded by wide margins. Large rolling mills and seamless steel tube plants at the Anshan Iron and Steel Company went into production; the First Automobile Works in Changchun produced New China's first domestic Jiefang (Liberation) truck; the Shenyang aircraft factory successfully trial-produced New China's first jet aircraft; and the First Tractor Plant in Luoyang and others began construction. The Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opened, and the Kang-Tibet, Qinghai-Tibet and Xinjiang-Tibet highways opened to traffic. China established a number of basic industries it had never had before. The plan's successful completion began to change China's industrial backwardness, laid a first foundation for socialist industrialization, and noticeably raised living standards.

events.title: Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence and Bandung Conference
events.short: Zhou Enlai first proposed the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence in late 1953, and at the 1955 Bandung Conference helped it succeed by "seeking common ground while reserving differences."
events.detail: After its founding New China followed an independent foreign policy of peace and worked to develop friendly relations with other countries. In December 1953, receiving an Indian government delegation, Premier Zhou Enlai first put forward five principles, mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, mutual non-aggression, non-interference in each other's internal affairs, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence, as the principles for handling relations between the two countries. In 1954 Zhou Enlai visited India and Burma, and China, India and Burma jointly advocated the Five Principles as the norms for international relations. They have since become a basic norm for relations between states, recognized by most countries of the world. In April 1955 delegates from 29 Asian and African countries and territories met at the Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia, and Zhou Enlai led the Chinese delegation. During the conference some attacked communism and sowed discord, creating disagreements and at one point even a danger of breakdown. In response Zhou made a supplementary speech putting forward the policy of "seeking common ground while reserving differences," saying: "The Chinese delegation has come to seek unity and not to quarrel... The Chinese delegation has come to seek common ground, not to create differences." His speech won general praise from the delegates and turned the conference from crisis to success. The conference adopted a final communique setting out ten principles for handling international relations and forming the "Bandung Spirit" of unity, anti-imperialism, anti-colonialism and the pursuit of national independence. After Bandung, China's relations with Asian and African countries developed further, and New China's international influence grew.

events.title: Geneva Conference
events.short: In 1954 New China attended the Geneva Conference for the first time as one of the five great powers, contributing to the restoration of peace in Indochina and showing its status as a major power.
events.detail: After the Korean armistice, to settle the Korean question and restore peace in Indochina by peaceful means, the foreign ministers of the Soviet Union, the United States, Britain and France decided in early 1954 to hold an international conference in Geneva, Switzerland, and invited the People's Republic of China to take part. From April to July 1954 the People's Republic attended the Geneva Conference for the first time as one of the five great powers, with Zhou Enlai leading the Chinese delegation. It was New China's first international conference to discuss major international questions. The conference took up the Korean question first, but because of US obstruction no agreement was reached. It then discussed Indochina, where Zhou Enlai worked actively through diplomacy to bring about an agreement. In July the conference reached the Geneva Accords on restoring peace in Indochina, providing for ceasefires in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia and the withdrawal of French forces from Indochina, which briefly quieted the fighting there. During the conference Zhou also carried out wide diplomatic activity outside the sessions, meeting representatives of Britain and other Western countries; China and Britain agreed to exchange chargés d'affaires, establishing semi-diplomatic relations. Zhou also held a reception for journalists from many countries at which he screened the Chinese color opera film Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai, introducing it as "China's Romeo and Juliet," and it was warmly received. The conference widened China's international influence, raised New China's standing, and showed the world its determination and ability to safeguard world peace. During it, Chinese and US representatives also began contacts, and ambassador-level talks started in 1955.

events.title: First National People's Congress and the 1954 Constitution
events.short: In September 1954 the First National People's Congress adopted New China's first constitution, making the people's congress system the country's fundamental political system.
events.detail: In New China's early years, conditions were not yet ripe, so the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference exercised the powers of the National People's Congress and the Common Program served as a provisional constitution. With economic construction and social stability, conditions for convening a National People's Congress and drafting a constitution gradually matured. In 1953 the country held its first census and its first large-scale general election. In January 1953 the Central People's Government set up a constitution drafting committee chaired by Mao Zedong, and after the draft was published it was discussed nationwide for over two months, with more than 150 million people taking part. From 15 to 28 September 1954 the First Session of the First National People's Congress met in Beijing, attended by over 1,200 deputies. It adopted the Constitution of the People's Republic of China, the country's first constitution of the socialist type. The constitution provided that the People's Republic of China is a people's democratic state led by the working class and based on the alliance of workers and peasants; that all power belongs to the people; and that the organs through which the people exercise power are the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at all levels. The session elected Mao Zedong chairman and Zhu De vice chairman of the People's Republic, Liu Shaoqi chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and approved Zhou Enlai as premier of the State Council. The convening of the first Congress and the promulgation of the constitution marked the formal establishment of the people's congress system nationwide as the fundamental political system.

events.title: Socialist Transformation Largely Completed
events.short: From 1953 China carried out socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce, largely completed by the end of 1956, establishing the basic socialist system.
events.detail: After the founding of New China, the country was in a period of transition from New Democracy to socialism. In 1953 the Party Central Committee formally put forward the general line for the transition period: over a fairly long time, to gradually achieve socialist industrialization and gradually carry out socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce, known as "one industrialization and three transformations." After land reform, peasants had land, but agriculture was still small-scale peasant farming by individual households. The state therefore guided peasants along the road of mutual aid and cooperation, from mutual-aid teams to elementary and then advanced agricultural cooperatives, gradually changing private ownership of the means of production to collective ownership. Handicrafts were also organized into cooperatives. For capitalist industry and commerce the state adopted a policy of peaceful redemption, using state-capitalist forms such as processing orders, state purchase and marketing, and joint state-private operation to turn capitalist private ownership gradually into socialist public ownership. In early 1956 a high tide of socialist transformation swept the country. In joint state-private enterprises, capitalists received a fixed interest of 5 percent a year on their shares. By the end of 1956 China had largely completed the socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce, the basic socialist system was preliminarily established, and China entered the primary stage of socialism. The transformations turned private ownership of the means of production into socialist public ownership, but they also suffered from problems such as excessive haste, crude work, changes made too fast and forms that were too simple and uniform.

events.title: On the Ten Major Relationships and the Eighth Party Congress
events.short: In 1956 Mao Zedong's On the Ten Major Relationships began the search for a Chinese path of development, and the Eighth CCP National Congress called for focusing on the productive forces.
events.detail: After socialist transformation was largely complete, the Communist Party began to explore a road of socialist construction suited to China's conditions. In February 1956 the 20th Congress of the Soviet Communist Party met and Khrushchev denounced Stalin, exposing some flaws in the Soviet model. The Party Central Committee recognized that Soviet experience could not simply be copied, and that China should take the Soviet Union as a mirror and find its own way. In April 1956 Mao Zedong delivered On the Ten Major Relationships at an enlarged meeting of the Politburo, discussing ten questions such as the relationship of heavy industry to light industry and agriculture, and calling for mobilizing all positive factors to serve the cause of socialism. It marked a good beginning of the Party's exploration of China's own road of socialist construction. That year Mao also put forward the policies of "Let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend" and of "long-term coexistence and mutual supervision." In September 1956 the Eighth National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party met in Beijing. It stated that the socialist system had largely been established in China, that the main contradiction at home was between the people's demand for an advanced industrial country and the reality of a backward agrarian one, and that the main task of the Party and the people was to concentrate on developing the productive forces and turn China as quickly as possible from a backward agrarian country into an advanced industrial one. It held to an economic construction policy of opposing both conservatism and rash advance and moving steadily forward in comprehensive balance, and stressed collective leadership, opposition to the personality cult and the development of inner-Party democracy. The line of the Eighth Congress was correct but was not well upheld afterward.

events.title: Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge Completed
events.short: Construction of the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge began in 1955 and it opened in October 1957, the first bridge across the Yangtze, turning a natural barrier into a thoroughfare.
events.detail: The Yangtze is China's longest river and historically a "natural moat" that cut off north-south travel. With no bridge, the Beijing-Hankou and Guangzhou-Hankou railways were severed by the river, and all goods and passengers going north or south had to cross by ferry. After New China's founding the Party and government decided to build the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge. Work began in September 1955, with technical aid from Soviet experts such as Sylin; the Chinese bridge expert Mao Yisheng chaired the technical advisory committee, and Peng Min, head of the Railway Ministry's Bridge Engineering Bureau, directed construction. The builders used the "caisson-pile drilling method," then the most advanced in the world, to overcome the deep, fast water and complex geology. After over two years of intense work the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opened on 15 October 1957. It is 1,670 meters long, with a main bridge of 1,156 meters, and is a double-deck road and rail bridge, with a highway on top and a double-track railway below; the main bridge has eight piers and nine spans. It was the first bridge across the Yangtze, and its completion linked the Beijing-Hankou and Guangzhou-Hankou railways into the north-south Beijing-Guangzhou Railway and joined the three towns of Wuhan into one. In 1956, while the bridge was under construction, Mao Zedong swam the Yangtze and wrote the lines "A single bridge flies from north to south, turning a natural barrier into a thoroughfare." The bridge was one of the key projects of the First Five-Year Plan and marked a new level in China's bridge-building technology. In 1968 the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge, designed and built by China itself, opened to traffic.

events.title: The Great Leap Forward and Economic Readjustment
events.short: The Great Leap Forward and people's communes launched in 1958 caused severe economic hardship; from 1961 a policy of readjusting, consolidating, filling out and raising standards followed.
events.detail: After socialist transformation was largely complete, the Chinese people were eager to change their country's economic and cultural backwardness. With too little experience in socialist construction and a rush for quick results, the role of subjective will and effort was exaggerated. In 1958 the second session of the Eighth Party Congress put forward the general line of "going all out, aiming high, and achieving greater, faster, better and more economical results in building socialism." A high tide of the "Great Leap Forward" then quickly swept every front, with unrealistic targets such as doubling steel output in a year to 10.7 million tons, which led to a nationwide campaign to smelt steel, while in agriculture "high-yield satellites" of grain were announced and exaggeration was rife. That same year the rural people's commune movement merged advanced agricultural cooperatives into people's communes and spread a "communist wind." Leftist errors marked by high targets, blind commanding, exaggeration and the "communist wind" spread widely. The Great Leap Forward and the commune movement disrupted the normal order of the national economy and caused serious imbalances; together with natural disasters and the withdrawal of Soviet experts, the economy fell into serious difficulties from 1959 to 1961, and the people suffered heavy losses. In January 1961 the Ninth Plenary Session of the Eighth Central Committee formally decided on the eight-character policy for the economy: "readjust, consolidate, fill out and raise standards." In January 1962 the Party Central Committee held an enlarged working conference, the "Seven Thousand Cadres Conference," which made a preliminary summing-up of lessons since the Great Leap Forward. After the readjustment, the economy had fully recovered and developed by 1965.

images.caption: Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Chen Yun at the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference, 1962

events.title: Democratic Reform in Tibet
events.short: In 1959 a reactionary clique in the Tibetan upper class launched an armed rebellion; after the central government put it down, democratic reform abolished feudal serfdom and freed a million serfs.
events.detail: After the peaceful liberation of Tibet, the feudal serfdom that united religion and government remained in place. Three major lords, government officials, nobles and upper-ranking monks of the monasteries, under 5 percent of the population, held most of Tibet's farmland, pastures and livestock, while serfs and slaves, over 90 percent of the population, had neither means of production nor personal freedom. Under the Seventeen Point Agreement, the Central People's Government took a very cautious attitude toward reforming Tibet's social system, deciding that reform would be carried out by the Tibetan local government itself, and in 1957 announced "no reform for six years." But the reactionary clique of the Tibetan upper class, to preserve feudal serfdom forever and with the backing of foreign anti-China forces, openly tore up the Seventeen Point Agreement in March 1959 and launched a full-scale armed rebellion in Lhasa, and the 14th Dalai Lama fled to India. The People's Liberation Army units stationed in Tibet were ordered to put down the rebellion swiftly. On 28 March 1959 the State Council ordered the dissolution of the Tibetan local government. The Party Central Committee then decided to carry out democratic reform in Tibet while suppressing the rebellion. The reform abolished the feudal serf-owners' land ownership and the feudal serfdom that united religion and government. By 1961 democratic reform in Tibet was largely complete: a million serfs gained personal freedom, received land and means of production, and became masters of the country and society. In September 1965 the Tibet Autonomous Region was formally established and regional ethnic autonomy began. Democratic reform was the most extensive and profound social change in Tibetan history. In 2009 the Tibet Autonomous Region's People's Congress designated 28 March as "Serfs Emancipation Day."

events.title: Daqing Oilfield Campaign and "Iron Man" Wang Jinxi
events.short: In the Daqing oil campaign begun in 1960, "Iron Man" Wang Jinxi led his drilling team through great hardship; by 1963 China was largely self-sufficient in oil.
events.detail: In New China's early years, China's oil industry was extremely backward, and some Western scholars asserted that China was "oil-poor." The geologist Li Siguang and others, relying on the theory of continental oil generation, held that the Songliao Plain in the Northeast offered good prospects. In September 1959 the third base well in the Songliao Basin struck commercial oil flow, discovering a major field named the Daqing Oilfield. In early 1960 the Party Central Committee decided to concentrate forces for a major oil campaign at Daqing, drawing tens of thousands of people from across the country. It was a time of economic hardship, and Daqing, on open wilderness with bitter winters, offered extremely harsh conditions, but "where there are conditions we go forward, and where there are none we create them and go forward." Wang Jinxi (1923–1970), leader of Drilling Team 1205, came to Daqing from the Yumen Oilfield. With no crane when the rig arrived, the team hauled it to the well site by hand and on their shoulders; when drilling began and water was short, they broke the ice to fetch water and carried it in basins to keep the drilling going. When a blowout occurred, Wang jumped into the mud pit despite his injured leg and stirred the mud with his body to bring it under control. He declared, "I would rather live twenty years less than fail to take this great oilfield," and people called him "Iron Man." After over three years of hard work the Daqing Oilfield was built and went into production. At the end of 1963 Zhou Enlai announced at the National People's Congress that China's oil needs were basically self-supplied. In 1964 Mao Zedong issued the call "In industry, learn from Daqing." The Daqing spirit of "patriotism, pioneering, realism and dedication" and the "Iron Man spirit" became a precious spiritual asset of the Chinese nation.

events.title: Learn from Comrade Lei Feng
events.short: On 5 March 1963 Mao Zedong inscribed "Learn from Comrade Lei Feng," sparking a nationwide drive to follow his spirit of serving the people wholeheartedly; 5 March became Learn from Lei Feng Day.
events.detail: With the growth of socialist construction, a fine social ethos of serving the people wholeheartedly and taking pleasure in helping others took shape, and many outstanding exemplars appeared, of whom Lei Feng was a leading example. Lei Feng (1940–1962), from Wangcheng, Hunan, was born into a poor peasant family and was orphaned at seven. He worked successively as a messenger, a tractor driver and a worker at Anshan Iron and Steel, and joined the People's Liberation Army in 1960 as a truck driver in a transport company of the Shenyang Military Region, joining the Communist Party the same year. Lei Feng loved the Party and the people, was diligent in his work and frugal in his life, and often helped comrades and civilians, doing countless good deeds; it was said that "on a thousand-li trip, he did a trainload of good deeds." He wrote in his diary: "A person's life is limited, but serving the people is limitless. I will devote my limited life to limitless service to the people." He promoted a "nail spirit" of squeezing out time for hard study, and was willing to be a "screw" of the revolution, loving whatever job he did. On 15 August 1962 Lei Feng died on duty while carrying out a task, at only 22. On 5 March 1963 the People's Daily and other papers published Mao Zedong's inscription "Learn from Comrade Lei Feng." A nationwide movement to learn from Lei Feng quickly arose, the Lei Feng spirit became a byword for serving the people wholeheartedly, and 5 March has since been "Learn from Lei Feng Day" each year. The Lei Feng spirit has influenced generation after generation of Chinese and is still carried forward. The Lei Feng Memorial Hall stands in Fushun, Liaoning.

events.title: First Atomic Bomb Test ("Two Bombs, One Satellite")
events.short: China exploded its first atomic bomb on 16 October 1964, followed by a hydrogen bomb and a satellite; the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" program greatly strengthened national defense.
events.detail: In the 1950s the United States and other nuclear powers repeatedly threatened China with nuclear weapons. To break the nuclear monopoly and nuclear blackmail and defend national security, in January 1955 the Party Central Committee made the strategic decision to develop atomic energy. In 1956 the state drew up the Long-Term Plan for the Development of Science and Technology, 1956–1967. A large group of scientists, represented by Qian Xuesen, Deng Jiaxian, Qian Sanqiang, Guo Yonghuai, Wang Ganchang and Zhu Guangya, devoted themselves to developing the "Two Bombs, One Satellite." In 1959 the Soviet government tore up its agreements, halted aid and withdrew its experts. To remember June 1959, when the Soviet agreement was torn up, the first atomic bomb was code-named "596." On 16 October 1964 China's first atomic bomb was successfully exploded at Lop Nur in the west, breaking the superpowers' nuclear monopoly. The Chinese government immediately declared solemnly that China would never be the first to use nuclear weapons at any time or under any circumstances. On 17 June 1967 China's first hydrogen bomb was successfully exploded; going from atomic bomb to hydrogen bomb took only two years and eight months. On 24 April 1970 China launched its first satellite, Dongfanghong 1, on a Long March 1 rocket. The success of the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" greatly strengthened China's national defense. In 1999 the state awarded the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" Meritorious Medal to 23 scientists and technical experts. Those involved formed the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" spirit of "loving the motherland and selfless dedication; self-reliance and hard struggle; close cooperation and daring to climb."

events.title: Synthesis of Crystalline Bovine Insulin
events.short: In 1965 Chinese scientists achieved the world's first synthesis of crystalline bovine insulin, the first biologically active protein made artificially, a world-leading result.
events.detail: Insulin is a protein hormone secreted by the islet cells of the pancreas that regulates blood sugar and can be used to treat diabetes. In 1955 the British scientist Frederick Sanger determined the full amino acid sequence of bovine insulin, which consists of two peptide chains, A and B, with 51 amino acids in all, and won the 1958 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for it. Because proteins carry out the main functions of life, synthesizing a protein was seen as a key step toward unlocking the secrets of life. In 1958 the Shanghai Institute of Biochemistry of the Chinese Academy of Sciences proposed the project of synthesizing insulin, and a joint team was formed with the Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry and the Department of Chemistry at Peking University. Despite inexperience, simple equipment and shortages of materials, the researchers first synthesized the A and B chains separately and then joined them. After over six years of hard work, on 17 September 1965 Chinese scientists were the first in the world to synthesize crystalline bovine insulin with the same biological activity as the natural hormone. It was the first biologically active protein synthesized artificially and marked a crucial step in understanding life and probing its secrets, leading the world at the time. The result was published in Kexue Tongbao in 1966. In 1981 Chinese scientists went on to achieve the first synthesis of yeast alanine transfer RNA. In this period Yuan Longping also began his research on hybrid rice in 1964.

events.title: The Cultural Revolution
events.short: The Cultural Revolution (1966–1976), wrongly launched by the leadership and exploited by counter-revolutionary cliques, brought severe disaster to the Party, the state and the people.
events.detail: In the mid-1960s Mao Zedong wrongly believed that the Party and the state faced a danger of capitalist restoration and stressed "taking class struggle as the key link." In May and August 1966 the Party Central Committee held an enlarged Politburo meeting and the Eleventh Plenary Session of the Eighth Central Committee, which adopted the May 16 Circular and the Decision on the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution, and the Cultural Revolution was fully launched. After it began, a Red Guard movement arose in many places, publicly denouncing "those in power taking the capitalist road" and "reactionary academic authorities," and many cadres and intellectuals were persecuted. In 1967 rebel groups in Shanghai seized Party and government power in the city, and a frenzy of "all-round seizure of power" swept the country, paralyzing Party and government organs at every level; head of state Liu Shaoqi was falsely accused and persecuted to death. In September 1971 the plot of the Lin Biao counter-revolutionary clique for an armed coup was exposed, and Lin Biao died in a plane crash while fleeing abroad. Zhou Enlai then took charge of the Central Committee's day-to-day work, and in 1975 Deng Xiaoping led a comprehensive rectification, improving the situation somewhat. In 1976 Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and Mao Zedong died in succession. In October 1976 the Politburo, represented by Hua Guofeng and Ye Jianying, smashed the Jiang Qing counter-revolutionary clique (the "Gang of Four") in one stroke, ending the Cultural Revolution disaster. The Cultural Revolution brought the Party, the state and the people their most severe setback and losses since the founding of New China. In 1981 the Sixth Plenary Session of the Eleventh Central Committee adopted the Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party Since the Founding of the People's Republic of China, which fully repudiated it.

The two clashed in 1962–1965, especially during the Four Cleanups campaign.

events.title: Founding of the Second Artillery Corps and Missile Forces
events.short: China founded the Second Artillery Corps, its strategic missile force, in July 1966; it was the core of China's strategic deterrent and was renamed the PLA Rocket Force in 2015.
events.detail: In the 1950s, facing nuclear threats and blackmail from the superpowers, the Party Central Committee decided to develop missiles and nuclear weapons. In 1956 the Fifth Academy of the Ministry of National Defense was founded, with Qian Xuesen as president, and began developing missiles. In 1957 China formed its first missile training unit. In November 1960 the Dongfeng-1, China's first short-range surface-to-surface missile, copied from a foreign design, was launched successfully. In June 1964 the Dongfeng-2, a medium-short-range missile of China's own design, was launched successfully. On 1 July 1966, with the approval of the Party Central Committee and the Central Military Commission, the leading organ of China's strategic missile forces was formally established, and Zhou Enlai named it the "Second Artillery." It comprised strategic nuclear surface-to-surface missile units, conventional missile units and support units, and was the core of China's strategic deterrent. On 27 October 1966 China successfully tested a nuclear missile on its own territory, achieving the combination of the "two bombs." The Second Artillery continued to grow, fielding medium-range, long-range and intercontinental strategic missiles as well as conventional missiles. In May 1980 China successfully launched a long-range rocket into a designated area of the South Pacific, demonstrating the long-range strike capability of its strategic missiles. China has consistently pursued a defensive national defense policy and a nuclear policy of no first use. On 31 December 2015 the Second Artillery was renamed the People's Liberation Army Rocket Force, a service on a par with the army, navy and air force. At the 2019 National Day parade for the 70th anniversary, new equipment such as the Dongfeng-41 intercontinental strategic nuclear missile made a public appearance.
