events.title: First Hydrogen Bomb Test
events.short: China's first hydrogen bomb was successfully air-dropped and exploded on 17 June 1967, only two years and eight months after its first atomic bomb, among the fastest in the world.
events.detail: A hydrogen bomb is a nuclear weapon that releases enormous energy through the fusion of light nuclei such as the hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium. It is also called a thermonuclear weapon, and is far more powerful than an atomic bomb. After the first atomic bomb was exploded, the Party Central Committee and Mao Zedong asked for the hydrogen bomb to be developed faster. Scientists represented by Yu Min, Deng Jiaxian, Peng Huanwu, Huang Zuqia and Zhou Guangzhao explored hydrogen bomb principles on their own strength, with no foreign materials to consult. In 1965 Yu Min led a research group in Shanghai doing calculations and found the key to achieving self-sustaining thermonuclear burning, producing a largely complete theoretical design from principle to configuration, known as the "Yu Min configuration." In December 1966 China conducted a hydrogen bomb principle test, which succeeded. On 17 June 1967 China's first hydrogen bomb, dropped from a bomber, was successfully exploded over Lop Nur in Xinjiang, with a yield of 3.3 megatons of TNT. From first atomic bomb to first hydrogen bomb, the United States took over seven years, the Soviet Union about four, Britain over four, and France over eight, while China took only two years and eight months, among the fastest in the world. The success marked a new stage in the development of China's nuclear weapons and further broke the superpowers' nuclear monopoly. The scientists involved long worked anonymously and in silence; Yu Min was unknown to the public for decades, received the State Preeminent Science and Technology Award in 2014 and the Medal of the Republic in 2019, and Deng Jiaxian is honored as a "founding father of the Two Bombs."

events.title: Dongfanghong 1 Satellite Launched
events.short: On 24 April 1970 China launched its first satellite, Dongfanghong 1, on a Long March 1 rocket, becoming the fifth country to launch a satellite independently.
events.detail: The Soviet Union launched the world's first satellite in 1957, and in 1958 Mao Zedong called for "we too must build satellites," and China's space technology grew from nothing. Under the leadership of scientists such as Qian Xuesen, Zhao Jiuzhang and Sun Jiadong, technicians worked despite scarce materials and simple equipment. In 1965 China formally began its satellite project, code-named "651," with the requirements that the satellite be able to "go up, be tracked, be heard and be seen." On 24 April 1970 China successfully launched its first satellite, Dongfanghong 1 (The East Is Red 1), on a Long March 1 rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The satellite weighed 173 kilograms, heavier than the first satellites of the Soviet Union, the United States, France and Japan combined, and played the tune The East Is Red in space. China thus became, after the Soviet Union, the United States, France and Japan, the fifth country to launch a satellite independently with its own rocket, marking its entry into the space age. The success of Dongfanghong 1, together with the atomic and hydrogen bombs, is known as the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" and greatly inspired the whole nation. China's space program then developed rapidly: a recoverable remote-sensing satellite in 1975, its first geostationary communications satellite in 1984, and the successful launch of the uncrewed Shenzhou 1 spacecraft in 1999. In 2016 the state designated 24 April as China Space Day each year. Dongfanghong 1 is still in orbit in space.

images.caption: Dongfanghong 1

events.title: First Nuclear Submarine Developed
events.short: China began developing nuclear submarines in 1958, and in 1974 its first, Long March 1, was delivered to the Navy, making China the fifth country with nuclear submarines.
events.detail: A nuclear submarine is powered by a nuclear reactor and can sail underwater for long periods, making it an important part of a country's strategic deterrent. On the eve of New China's founding, the first naval unit of the People's Liberation Army, the East China Military Region Navy, was established at Baimamiao in Taizhou, Jiangsu, and the People's Navy was born. To break the superpowers' nuclear monopoly and blackmail, in 1958 the Party Central Committee approved development of a missile nuclear submarine. In 1959 Khrushchev refused to give China technical assistance on nuclear submarines, and Mao Zedong said firmly: "Nuclear submarines, even if it takes ten thousand years, we must build them!" Researchers represented by Peng Shilu and Huang Xuhua, with no blueprints and no materials, started from zero and relied on their own efforts, doing their calculations with abacuses and slide rules. In December 1970 China's first nuclear submarine was launched at Huludao, Liaoning. On 1 August 1974 it was named Long March 1 and formally handed over to the Navy, making China, after the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain and France, the fifth country with nuclear submarines. In 1988 China's nuclear submarine successfully completed an extreme-depth dive test and an underwater rocket launch test. Huang Xuhua lived anonymously for thirty years, is hailed as the "father of China's nuclear submarines," and received the Medal of the Republic in 2019. The success strengthened China's national defense and its strategic deterrence at sea. Long March 1 was retired in 2013 and is now on display at the PLA Navy Museum.

events.title: September 13 Incident
events.short: In September 1971 the Lin Biao clique's plot for an armed coup was exposed, and on 13 September Lin Biao and others fled by plane and died in a crash at Öndörkhaan, Mongolia.
events.detail: After the Cultural Revolution began, Lin Biao's standing rose rapidly, and in 1969 the Ninth Party Congress wrote into the Party constitution that Lin was Mao Zedong's "successor." A counter-revolutionary clique then formed around Lin, plotting a coup to seize supreme power in the Party and state. In 1970, at the Second Plenary Session of the Ninth Central Committee, the Lin clique made trouble over the question of restoring the post of head of state and was criticized by Mao. In March 1971 Lin's son Lin Liguo and others drew up an armed coup plan, the Outline of Project 571. From August to September Mao toured the south. Learning of this, the Lin clique decided to murder Mao on his return trip to Beijing and launch an armed coup. Mao sensed something was wrong, changed his itinerary and returned safely to Beijing ahead of schedule, and the plot failed. The plan of Lin and others to flee south to Guangzhou and set up a rival central government also came to nothing. In the early hours of 13 September 1971 Lin Biao, Ye Qun, Lin Liguo and others hurriedly fled in a Trident aircraft from Shanhaiguan airport, flying toward the Soviet Union; the plane crashed near Öndörkhaan in Mongolia and everyone aboard was killed, in what is known as the "September 13 Incident." Zhou Enlai responded calmly and took decisive measures to stabilize the situation. The incident marked the failure of the theory and practice of the Cultural Revolution. Zhou Enlai then took charge of the Central Committee's day-to-day work, and things took a turn for the better in many areas. In 1980–1981 a special tribunal of the Supreme People's Court tried the principal members of the Lin Biao and Jiang Qing counter-revolutionary cliques according to law.

events.title: Restoration of China's Seat at the United Nations
events.short: On 25 October 1971 the 26th UN General Assembly passed Resolution 2758 by an overwhelming majority, restoring all the lawful rights of the People's Republic of China in the United Nations.
events.detail: The United Nations was founded in 1945 as an international organization of sovereign states. China was one of its founding members and a permanent member of the Security Council. After the People's Republic was founded it should have held China's lawful seat, but because of obstruction by the United States and other Western countries, the Taiwan authorities occupied China's seat for a long time. From 1950 the Chinese government and friendly countries repeatedly proposed at the General Assembly that the People's Republic's lawful seat be restored, and each time the United States and others blocked it. On 25 October 1971 the 26th General Assembly passed Resolution 2758, proposed by 23 countries including Albania and Algeria, by an overwhelming vote of 76 in favor, 35 against and 17 abstentions. It decided to restore all the rights of the People's Republic of China, to recognize the representatives of its government as the only lawful representatives of China to the United Nations, and to expel immediately the representatives of the Taiwan authorities from the United Nations and all its related organizations. When the result was announced, delegates of many countries applauded warmly. Mao Zedong said: "It was our African friends who carried us into the United Nations." In November a Chinese delegation led by Qiao Guanhua attended the 26th General Assembly. China's restoration of its lawful seat was a major diplomatic victory for New China and greatly raised China's international standing and influence. Resolution 2758 settled, politically, legally and procedurally, the question of the representation of all of China, including Taiwan, in the United Nations.

events.title: Ping-Pong Diplomacy and Nixon's Visit to China
events.short: "Ping-pong diplomacy" in 1971 opened the door to contact between China and the United States, and Nixon's 1972 visit led to the Shanghai Communique and the start of normalization of relations.
events.detail: After New China's founding, the US government was hostile to it and followed a policy of blockade, embargo and encirclement, and relations between the two countries remained adversarial for a long time. In the late 1960s and early 1970s the international situation changed, and both countries needed better relations. In April 1971 the American table tennis team, in Nagoya, Japan, for the 31st World Table Tennis Championships, was invited to visit China, and Zhou Enlai received them, saying: "Your visit at our invitation has opened the door to friendly contacts between the peoples of our two countries." This was the famous "ping-pong diplomacy," described as "the small ball moving the big ball." In July the US national security adviser Henry Kissinger secretly visited China and held talks with Zhou Enlai to prepare for a presidential visit. In February 1972 President Richard Nixon visited China and was received by Mao Zedong. On 28 February the two sides signed the Joint Communique of the United States and China in Shanghai, known as the Shanghai Communique, in which the United States stated: "The United States acknowledges that all Chinese on either side of the Taiwan Strait maintain there is but one China and that Taiwan is a part of China. The United States Government does not challenge that position." The communique marked the start of normalization of relations and ended more than twenty years of confrontation. Nixon called the visit "the week that changed the world." The easing of Sino-US relations spurred China's relations with Western countries and set off another wave of diplomatic recognition after New China's founding. On 1 January 1979 China and the United States formally established diplomatic relations.

events.title: China–Japan Diplomatic Normalization
events.short: In September 1972 Japanese Prime Minister Kakuei Tanaka visited China, and the two countries issued a joint communiqué normalizing relations; many other countries then established ties with China.
events.detail: After the Second World War, Japan followed the United States in opposing the new China and maintained so-called “diplomatic relations” with the Taiwan authorities, so China and Japan long had no formal diplomatic ties. From the 1950s the two countries developed non-governmental trade and cultural exchanges, and in 1962 they signed the Memorandum on Long-Term Comprehensive Trade. After Nixon’s visit to China, calls in Japan to restore Japan–China relations grew louder. In July 1972 Kakuei Tanaka became Japan’s prime minister, and in September he visited China at its invitation. On 29 September the two governments issued the China–Japan Joint Communiqué, ending the abnormal state of affairs that had existed between them and establishing diplomatic relations. Japan expressed its keen awareness of its responsibility for the serious damage its wartime actions had caused the Chinese people and its deep self-reproach; it recognized the government of the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal government of China and fully understood and respected China’s position that Taiwan is an inalienable part of its territory. China declared that, for the sake of friendship between the two peoples, it renounced its demand for war reparations from Japan. Normalization opened a new era in relations. To mark it, China gave Japan a pair of giant pandas, Kang Kang and Lan Lan. In 1978 the two countries signed the Treaty of Peace and Friendship, and Deng Xiaoping visited Japan. Around the time of normalization many countries established relations with China, and by the late 1970s more than one hundred had done so.

events.title: Tu Youyou Discovers Artemisinin
events.short: In the early 1970s Tu Youyou’s team, inspired by an ancient medical text, extracted the antimalarial artemisinin from sweet wormwood, saving millions of lives; she won a Nobel Prize in 2015.
events.detail: Malaria is an infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and spread by mosquitoes. In the 1960s the parasites developed resistance to quinine-type drugs, and many countries mobilized researchers to find new antimalarials. In 1967 China launched a national antimalarial research project code-named “523.” In 1969 Tu Youyou of the Institute of Chinese Materia Medica at the Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine became head of a research group and began studying antimalarial herbal remedies. She and her team systematically went through medical texts of past dynasties and collected more than 2,000 prescriptions. Extracts of sweet wormwood (qinghao) showed some antimalarial effect, but inconsistently. Tu drew inspiration from a line in A Handbook of Prescriptions for Emergencies (Zhouhou Beiji Fang) by Ge Hong of the Eastern Jin: “Take a handful of qinghao, soak it in two sheng of water, wring out the juice and drink it all.” She therefore switched to extraction with ether, which has a lower boiling point. In October 1971 the neutral ether extract of qinghao achieved a 100 percent inhibition rate against malaria in mice and monkeys. In 1972 the group isolated the active compound and named it qinghaosu (artemisinin). Artemisinin and its derivatives are highly effective, fast-acting and of low toxicity against falciparum malaria and other forms, and artemisinin-based combination therapies are recommended by the World Health Organization as the first-line treatment, saving millions of lives worldwide, especially in Africa. In 2015 Tu won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, becoming the first China-based scientist to win a Nobel science prize. The discovery was a major contribution of traditional Chinese medicine to human health.

events.title: Yuan Longping Develops Indica Hybrid Rice
events.short: In 1973 Yuan Longping’s team successfully bred indica hybrid rice, greatly raising rice yields and contributing enormously to solving food problems in China and around the world.
events.detail: Yuan Longping (1930–2021), a native of De’an, Jiangxi, was born in Beijing and spent many years teaching at Anjiang Agricultural School in Hunan. In the early 1960s China suffered severe food shortages, and Yuan resolved to defeat hunger with agricultural science. At the time it was held internationally that rice is a self-pollinating crop with no hybrid vigor. In 1964 Yuan found naturally male-sterile rice plants in the experimental field at Anjiang and began researching hybrid rice. In 1966 he published the paper “Male Sterility in Rice,” proposing breeding hybrid rice with a matched “three-line” system. In 1970 his assistant Li Bihu and others found a wild rice plant with aborted pollen in Sanya, Hainan, which Yuan named “Wild Abortive” (yeba) and which opened the breakthrough. With the cooperation of many research institutions, in 1973 Yuan’s team completed the matched “three lines” of male-sterile, maintainer and restorer lines and successfully bred indica hybrid rice. It yields about 20 percent more than conventional rice; planting began to spread nationwide in 1976, and by the end of the 20th century hybrid rice had added several hundred billion kilograms of grain in total. Yuan later proposed the “two-line method” and researched super hybrid rice. Hybrid rice also spread to many countries in Asia, Africa and the Americas, contributing enormously to solving the world’s food problems. Yuan is hailed as the “Father of Hybrid Rice”; in 2000 he won the first State Preeminent Science and Technology Award, and in 2019 the Medal of the Republic. He died in Changsha in May 2021.

events.title: Tiananmen Incident and Fall of the Gang of Four
events.short: In April 1976 mourning for Zhou Enlai grew into the April Fifth Movement against the Gang of Four; in October the Gang was smashed, ending the Cultural Revolution.
events.detail: During the Cultural Revolution, Jiang Qing, Wang Hongwen, Zhang Chunqiao and Yao Wenyuan gradually joined forces and plotted to seize Party and state power; Mao Zedong called them the “Gang of Four.” On 8 January 1976 Premier Zhou Enlai died, and people across the country mourned him deeply. The Gang suppressed the mourning, which aroused intense public anger. Around the Qingming Festival, hundreds of thousands of people gathered spontaneously in Tiananmen Square in Beijing to mourn Zhou and denounce the Gang, and lines such as “I want to grieve, but hear the demons howl; I weep while wolves and jackals laugh. I shed tears to honor a hero; with brows raised, I draw my sword” were widely recited. The Gang slandered the mourning as a “counter-revolutionary incident,” suppressed it, and used the occasion to strip Deng Xiaoping of all his posts. Known as the “April Fifth Movement,” the event laid the popular foundation for the Gang’s later fall. Zhu De died on 6 July 1976; on 28 July a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Tangshan, Hebei, killing over 240,000 people; and on 9 September Mao Zedong died. The Gang stepped up its efforts to seize supreme power. At this critical moment, the Political Bureau of the Central Committee, represented by Hua Guofeng and Ye Jianying, took decisive action on 6 October 1976, placing Wang Hongwen, Zhang Chunqiao, Jiang Qing and Yao Wenyuan under isolation and investigation. In one stroke the Gang of Four was smashed, ending the ten-year Cultural Revolution. People across the country rejoiced. Their fall ushered China into a new period of historical development. In 1978 the Central Committee decided to rehabilitate the April Fifth Movement.

events.title: Tangshan Earthquake
events.short: On 28 July 1976 a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Tangshan, Hebei, killing more than 240,000 people; the whole country rallied to support relief and reconstruction.
events.detail: At 3:42 a.m. on 28 July 1976 a powerful earthquake of magnitude 7.8 on the Richter scale (about 7.5 in moment magnitude) struck Tangshan, Hebei, with its epicenter in the urban area. At 6:45 p.m. that day a strong 7.1 aftershock hit nearby. The quake came while people were asleep and, in little more than ten seconds, nearly flattened an industrial city of a million people: buildings collapsed in great numbers, and transport, communications, water and power were all cut off, with Tianjin, Beijing and other places also affected. It killed 242,769 people and seriously injured more than 160,000, making it one of the deadliest earthquakes of the 20th century. The Party Central Committee and State Council quickly organized relief; more than 100,000 People’s Liberation Army officers and soldiers, with medical teams and engineers from across the country, rushed to Tangshan, and many soldiers dug through rubble with their bare hands to rescue the buried. Most of the more than ten thousand miners trapped underground at the Kailuan coal mine were saved. The people of Tangshan rebuilt through self-reliance and hard work. By 1986 a new Tangshan with a rational layout and full functions had largely been completed, and the city received the United Nations Habitat Scroll of Honour. The earthquake also advanced China’s seismological research and disaster-reduction work, and stricter seismic building standards followed. Today Tangshan has the Tangshan Earthquake Memorial Monument and the Earthquake Ruins Memorial Park, where people mourn the victims every year on 28 July. The “spirit of earthquake resistance” (selflessness, sharing hardship, perseverance and pressing forward) has inspired generation after generation.

events.title: Reinstatement of the College Entrance Exam
events.short: In 1977, under Deng Xiaoping, the college entrance exam was restored after a ten-year break; 5.7 million sat it that winter, putting higher education back on track.
events.detail: After the Cultural Revolution began, schools were forced to “suspend classes to make revolution,” and college admissions also halted. After 1970 some universities resumed enrollment but abolished examinations, using instead a recommendation system of “voluntary application, recommendation by the masses, approval by leaders and review by the school” to admit “worker-peasant-soldier students,” and educational quality fell sharply. In 1977 Deng Xiaoping, who had returned to work, volunteered to take charge of science, technology and education. In August, at a forum on science and education, he heard scientists’ and educators’ proposals to restore the entrance exam and decided on the spot to do so that very year. He said: “This year we must resolve to recruit students directly from high-school graduates, and stop the recommendation system.” In October the State Council approved the Ministry of Education’s Opinions on the 1977 University Admissions Work, announcing the restoration of the unified national entrance examination, with voluntary registration, a unified exam and admission by merit. In the winter of 1977, 5.7 million people sat the exam and more than 270,000 were admitted; in the summer of 1978 another 6.1 million took it. The restoration brought renewed respect for knowledge and talent, selected many outstanding people for the country and changed the fate of millions of young people. In March 1978 the National Science Conference was held, where Deng put forward that “science and technology are productive forces” and that “intellectuals are part of the working class,” ushering in the “spring of science.” Restoring the exam was an important breakthrough in setting right the wrongs of the previous years and had a profound impact on China’s modernization.

events.title: Debate on the Criterion of Truth
events.short: In 1978 the article “Practice Is the Sole Criterion for Testing Truth” set off a great debate on the criterion of truth, breaking the “Two Whatevers” fetters and advancing the liberation of thought.
events.detail: After the fall of the Gang of Four, people across the country demanded that the errors of the Cultural Revolution be corrected and unjust cases redressed. But the main leader of the Party Central Committee at the time put forward the “Two Whatevers” policy: “We will resolutely uphold whatever decisions Chairman Mao made, and unswervingly follow whatever instructions Chairman Mao gave.” This seriously obstructed the work of setting things right. Deng Xiaoping stated plainly that the “Two Whatevers” did not accord with Marxism and called for a complete and accurate understanding of Mao Zedong Thought. On 11 May 1978 Guangming Daily published, under the byline of a special commentator, the article “Practice Is the Sole Criterion for Testing Truth,” approved by Hu Yaobang; the next day the People’s Daily and other papers reprinted it. It argued that the only criterion for testing truth is social practice. It fundamentally refuted the “Two Whatevers,” provoked a strong response nationwide and set off a great debate on the criterion of truth. After the debate began, it was criticized and suppressed by supporters of the “Two Whatevers.” Leaders including Deng Xiaoping, Ye Jianying and Li Xiannian clearly backed it, and Deng said: “If a party, a country or a nation goes by the book in everything, thinks rigidly and lets superstition spread, it cannot move forward, its vitality will cease, and the party and the nation will perish.” The debate was a movement of Marxist liberation of thought. It broke the grip of the “Two Whatevers,” prepared the ground for the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee, and became the forerunner of the great historical turning point for the Party and the country.

events.title: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee
events.short: In December 1978 the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee decided to shift the focus to economic construction and adopt reform and opening-up, a great historical turning point.
events.detail: After the fall of the Gang of Four, people eagerly hoped for a new path of socialist development. From November to December 1978 the Central Committee held a work conference, at whose closing Deng Xiaoping delivered the speech “Emancipate the Mind, Seek Truth from Facts and Unite as One in Looking to the Future,” which in effect became the keynote report of the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee that followed. From 18 to 22 December 1978 the plenum was held in Beijing. It thoroughly repudiated the erroneous “Two Whatevers” policy, highly praised the debate on the criterion of truth, and reestablished the ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts. It ended the erroneous slogan of “taking class struggle as the key link,” and made the great decision to shift the focus of the work of the Party and the state to economic construction and to implement reform and opening-up. It also examined and resolved a number of major historical questions and the merits and demerits of some important leaders, rehabilitating those involved in the Tiananmen Incident and others, and added Chen Yun to the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau, forming a second-generation central leadership with Deng Xiaoping at its core. The plenum was a turning point of far-reaching significance in the Party’s history since 1949, opening a new period of reform, opening-up and socialist modernization. In the four-plus decades that followed, China’s economy rose to second in the world and living standards improved greatly. In 2018 a grand meeting was held to celebrate the 40th anniversary of reform and opening-up.

events.title: Xiaogang Village and Household Contracting
events.short: In 1978 eighteen farming households in Xiaogang Village, Anhui, secretly signed a “contract everything to households” pact, opening rural reform that then spread nationwide.
events.detail: After the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee, reform began in the countryside. Under the people’s commune system, peasants had little incentive to produce and grain output stagnated for years. Xiaogang Village in Fengyang County, Anhui, was a well-known “three-reliances village”: it relied on resold grain for food, on relief for money and on loans for production. In the winter of 1978, eighteen households there secretly signed a contract in a thatched hut and pressed their red fingerprints on it, agreeing to divide the collective land among households to farm (“contracting everything to households,” dabaogan); they agreed that if cadres were jailed for it, the members would raise their children until the age of 18. The next year Xiaogang had a bumper harvest, with a total grain output equal to the sum of the five years from 1966 to 1970, ending more than twenty years of reliance on relief grain. The practice was at first controversial, but Deng Xiaoping clearly supported it and affirmed contracting output to households. From 1982 to 1986 the Central Committee issued “No. 1 Documents” on agriculture, rural areas and farmers for five consecutive years, endorsing the household responsibility system. Under it, land stays publicly owned but is contracted to farm households, who deliver their quota to the state, set aside what is due the collective, and keep the rest. It stimulated peasants’ enthusiasm, freed rural productive forces and raised grain output sharply; in 1984 national output exceeded 400 million tons, basically solving the problem of feeding the population. After 1983 the people’s communes were gradually replaced by township governments. Xiaogang is hailed as the “birthplace of China’s rural reform.”

events.title: Establishment of China–US Diplomatic Relations
events.short: China and the US issued a communiqué in December 1978 and formally established diplomatic relations on 1 January 1979, the US recognizing one China; Deng Xiaoping visited the US that year.
events.detail: After Nixon’s 1972 visit to China and the Shanghai Communiqué, relations between the two countries began to normalize, and in 1973 they set up liaison offices in each other’s capitals. In 1978 the two sides negotiated on establishing diplomatic relations, with China insisting that the US meet three conditions regarding the Taiwan authorities: sever diplomatic relations, abrogate the treaty and withdraw troops. On 16 December 1978 China and the US simultaneously issued the Joint Communiqué on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations, announcing mutual recognition and diplomatic relations from 1 January 1979. The US recognized the government of the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal government of China, and acknowledged China’s position that there is but one China and that Taiwan is part of China. The two countries formally established relations on 1 January 1979. At the same time the US announced that it would sever so-called “diplomatic relations” with the Taiwan authorities, terminate the US–Taiwan Mutual Defense Treaty and withdraw US forces from Taiwan. The establishment of relations was a milestone, ending thirty years of abnormality. From January to February 1979 Deng Xiaoping visited the United States at its invitation, the first visit by a leader of the People’s Republic. In 1982 the two countries issued the August 17 Communiqué, in which the US pledged gradually to reduce arms sales to Taiwan. The Shanghai Communiqué, the Joint Communiqué on Establishing Diplomatic Relations and the August 17 Communiqué form the political foundation of China–US relations.

events.title: Message to Taiwan and One Country, Two Systems
events.short: On New Year’s Day 1979 the NPC Standing Committee issued the Message to Compatriots in Taiwan proposing cross-strait “three links”; Deng Xiaoping later put forward “one country, two systems.”
events.detail: After the founding of the People’s Republic, the Party and government made reunifying Taiwan with the mainland a sacred mission. On 1 January 1979 the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress issued the Message to Compatriots in Taiwan, announcing the major policy of peaceful reunification, proposing that the two sides quickly open postal, transport and trade links (the “three links”), and announcing a halt to shelling of Jinmen and other islands. In September 1981 Ye Jianying, chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, made a statement further setting out nine policies on Taiwan’s return and peaceful reunification (the “Ye Nine Points”), proposing that after reunification Taiwan could become a special administrative region with a high degree of autonomy and could keep its own armed forces. In 1982 Deng Xiaoping clearly put forward the concept of “one country, two systems” when meeting foreign guests. Its basic content is that, within the People’s Republic of China, the mainland upholds the socialist system while Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao keep their existing capitalist systems and ways of life unchanged for a long time. The 1982 Constitution provides that the state may establish special administrative regions when necessary, giving “one country, two systems” a legal basis. “Peaceful reunification, one country, two systems” became China’s basic policy for resolving the Taiwan question. The concept was first applied successfully to Hong Kong and Macao. In 2005 the National People’s Congress passed the Anti-Secession Law, which states in legal form the Chinese people’s firm will to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. Achieving complete national reunification is the shared wish of all Chinese people.

events.title: Special Economic Zones Established
events.short: In 1980 China set up special economic zones at Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen as windows on the world; Shenzhen grew from a small fishing town into a modern metropolis.
events.detail: After the Third Plenary Session, China took steps toward opening to the outside world. To attract foreign capital, bring in advanced technology and management experience and expand exports, in 1979 the Party Central Committee and State Council approved special policies and flexible measures for Guangdong and Fujian and decided to try out “export special zones” at Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen. In August 1980 the Standing Committee of the Fifth National People’s Congress approved the Regulations on Special Economic Zones in Guangdong Province, formally establishing zones at Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Shantou, and in October it approved the Xiamen zone as well. The zones applied special economic policies and management systems, relied mainly on foreign investment, were built mainly on joint ventures, cooperative ventures and wholly foreign-owned enterprises, and produced mainly for export. They became China’s windows on the world and “testing grounds” for reform and opening-up. Shenzhen was originally a border town of just over 30,000 people. After the zone was established, the Shekou Industrial Zone raised the slogan “Time is money, efficiency is life” and created “Shenzhen speed,” building a floor every three days. After decades of development Shenzhen has become an international metropolis of more than 17 million people. The zones greatly advanced reform, opening-up and socialist modernization. In 1984, after touring Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Xiamen, Deng Xiaoping inscribed: “The development and experience of Shenzhen prove that our policy of establishing special economic zones is correct.” In 2019 the Central Committee and State Council backed Shenzhen in building a pilot demonstration area of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

events.title: Setting Things Right and the History Resolution
events.short: After 1978 unjust cases were redressed and wrongs set right; the 1981 Resolution on Party History fully repudiated the Cultural Revolution and gave an assessment of Mao Zedong.
events.detail: Alongside the tide of liberated thinking, work to redress unjust, false and wrongly decided cases began nationwide. During the Cultural Revolution large numbers of cadres and ordinary people were persecuted, producing countless such cases. Under Hu Yaobang and others, the Organization Department of the Party Central Committee carried out the work comprehensively; by the end of 1982 more than three million cases had been redressed and over 470,000 Party members had their membership restored. In 1980 the Fifth Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee fully rehabilitated Liu Shaoqi, restoring the reputation of the head of state who had died after being wronged. In 1980–1981 a Special Court of the Supreme People’s Court tried the principal members of the Lin Biao and Jiang Qing counter-revolutionary cliques in public. To sum up the experience and lessons since 1949, in June 1981 the Sixth Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee adopted the Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party Since the Founding of the People’s Republic of China. It summarized the Party’s major historical events since 1949, fully repudiated the theory and practice of the Cultural Revolution, and assessed Mao Zedong’s historical standing, concluding that his achievements were primary and his errors secondary, and affirmed the great significance of Mao Zedong Thought as the Party’s guiding ideology. Its adoption marked the successful completion of the task of setting things right in guiding ideology.

events.title: 12th and 13th Party Congresses
events.short: In 1982 Deng Xiaoping called for “building socialism with Chinese characteristics”; in 1987 the 13th Party Congress set out the primary stage of socialism and the Party’s basic line.
events.detail: After the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee, Deng Xiaoping led the Communist Party in making a series of major decisions that pushed reform, opening-up and socialist modernization forward. In September 1982 the 12th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. In his opening speech Deng said: “Integrate the universal truth of Marxism with the concrete realities of China, find our own path and build socialism with Chinese characteristics: this is the basic conclusion we have drawn from long historical experience.” The Congress set the strategic goal of quadrupling the gross annual output value of industry and agriculture by the end of the 20th century. In October 1987 the 13th National Congress was held. It systematically set out the theory of the primary stage of socialism, holding that China was then in that stage. It laid down the Party’s basic line for that stage: to lead and unite the people of all ethnic groups in focusing on economic development, upholding the Four Cardinal Principles and persisting in reform and opening-up, striving to build China into a prosperous, democratic and culturally advanced modern socialist country, summed up as “one central task, two basic points.” It also put forward a “three-step” strategy for economic development: meet basic needs, reach a moderately prosperous level, and basically achieve modernization by the middle of the 21st century. The two Congresses charted the course for building socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Deng Xiaoping Theory gradually took shape; in 1997 the 15th Congress established it as the Party’s guiding ideology.

events.title: Urban Economic Reform
events.short: In October 1984 the Third Plenum of the 12th Central Committee adopted the Decision on Economic Structural Reform, shifting reform’s focus from countryside to cities and invigorating enterprises.
events.detail: Success in the countryside laid the foundation for deeper reform, and the wave of reform spread from rural areas to cities. Under the highly centralized planned economy, state-owned enterprises were appendages of the government, lacked autonomy and were inefficient, and the economy lacked vitality. In October 1984 the Third Plenary Session of the 12th Central Committee adopted the Decision on Economic Structural Reform, which stated that the socialist economy is a planned commodity economy based on public ownership. This broke with the traditional view that set the planned economy against the commodity economy, and marked a shift in the focus of reform from the countryside to cities as economic reform unfolded across the board. Urban reform took invigorating enterprises as its central link: separating government from enterprise management, separating ownership from management to a suitable degree, expanding enterprise autonomy, and introducing contract management and the factory director (manager) responsibility system so that enterprises ran themselves and bore their own profits and losses. Public ownership remained dominant while individual, private and foreign-funded sectors were allowed and encouraged to develop together. Self-employed traders and private businesses appeared in large numbers, with Nian Guangjiu’s “Fool’s Melon Seeds” a well-known example. In 1986 China promulgated the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law (Trial), and the Shenyang Explosion-Proof Equipment Factory became the first state-owned enterprise to go bankrupt in the People’s Republic. Urban reform invigorated enterprises, promoted the commodity economy and clearly raised material and cultural living standards, though problems such as rising prices also appeared.

events.title: Opening of Coastal Cities and Open Economic Zones
events.short: In 1984 China opened 14 coastal port cities, and from 1985 it created coastal open economic zones such as the Yangtze River Delta, gradually forming an all-round opening to the outside world.
events.detail: The success of the special economic zones gave experience for broader opening. In 1984, after touring Shenzhen and other zones, Deng Xiaoping suggested opening a few more port cities. That year China further opened 14 coastal port cities: Dalian, Qinhuangdao, Tianjin, Yantai, Qingdao, Lianyungang, Nantong, Shanghai, Ningbo, Wenzhou, Fuzhou, Guangzhou, Zhanjiang and Beihai, where some of the preferential policies of the special economic zones applied. These cities went on to set up economic and technological development zones. From 1985 China also designated the Yangtze River Delta, the Pearl River Delta and the Xiamen–Zhangzhou–Quanzhou triangle in southern Fujian as coastal open economic zones, later extended to the Liaodong and Shandong peninsulas and elsewhere. In 1990 the Central Committee and State Council decided to develop and open up Pudong in Shanghai. China then opened cities along the Yangtze and its borders and inland provincial capitals, gradually forming a multi-level, all-round pattern of opening from south to north and east to west. Opening promoted rapid growth: foreign capital poured in, foreign trade expanded quickly, living standards kept rising, and China also learned advanced science, technology and management from abroad. In 2001 China joined the World Trade Organization, and opening entered a new stage. From 2013 China set up free trade pilot zones starting with Shanghai and put forward the Belt and Road Initiative, promoting a new pattern of all-round opening. Opening to the outside world has become a basic national policy.

images.caption: Map of opening-up in China’s coastal areas

events.title: Sino-British Joint Declaration on Hong Kong
events.short: In December 1984 China and Britain signed a joint declaration confirming China would resume sovereignty over Hong Kong on 1 July 1997, putting “one country, two systems” into practice.
events.detail: Hong Kong has been Chinese territory since ancient times. In modern times Britain took Hong Kong Island and the southern tip of the Kowloon Peninsula and forcibly leased the “New Territories” for 99 years. In September 1982 British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher visited China, and in talks with her Deng Xiaoping made clear that sovereignty was not a matter for discussion and that China would take Hong Kong back in 1997: “If China did not take Hong Kong back in 1997, forty-eight years after the founding of the People’s Republic, no Chinese leader or government could answer to the Chinese people.” After twenty-two rounds of difficult negotiations, the Joint Declaration of the Governments of China and Britain on the Question of Hong Kong was formally signed in Beijing on 19 December 1984. It confirmed that China would resume the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong on 1 July 1997; China’s basic policies were that, under the principle of “one country, two systems,” a Hong Kong Special Administrative Region would be established with “Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong” and a high degree of autonomy, and that Hong Kong’s existing capitalist social and economic systems and way of life would remain unchanged for fifty years. In 1987 China and Portugal signed a joint declaration on Macao, confirming that China would resume sovereignty over Macao on 20 December 1999. In 1990 the National People’s Congress adopted the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Joint Declaration marked the first success of “one country, two systems” over Hong Kong and offered a new model for the peaceful settlement of international disputes.

events.title: Million-Strong Troop Reduction
events.short: In 1985 the Central Military Commission decided to cut the armed forces by one million, largely completed by 1987, setting the People’s Liberation Army on a path to a leaner force.
events.detail: Entering the 1980s, Party and state leaders correctly foresaw that a world war would not break out for the time being and that peace and development were the themes of the age. On this judgment China adjusted its guiding thinking on national defense, shifting from preparing for an early, large-scale nuclear war to a track of peacetime construction. Since 1949 the People’s Liberation Army had been large, with bloated organizations, excess personnel and low efficiency, and its total strength stood at over four million. In June 1985 an enlarged meeting of the Central Military Commission was held in Beijing, where Deng Xiaoping announced that the PLA would reduce its strength by one million. Over the next two years the army abolished or merged a large number of organizations at army level and above, merged the original eleven military regions into seven, reorganized armies into group armies, trimmed headquarters and non-combat personnel, and transferred some units to local authorities. By 1987 the reduction was basically complete, with total strength down to about 3.2 million. It streamlined the structure, improved the organization and raised combat capability, putting the PLA on a path to a lean force with Chinese characteristics and speeding its revolutionization, modernization and regularization. The cuts also lightened the state’s economic burden, helped concentrate efforts on economic construction and showed the world China’s sincerity in safeguarding peace. In 1988 the PLA restored its system of military ranks. China later made further reductions in 1997, 2003 and 2015, slimming the force toward a lean, joint and efficient military.

events.title: The 863 Program and the 973 Program
events.short: In 1986 four scientists proposed tracking world high technology, leading to the “863 Program”; the “973 Program” followed in 1997, boosting scientific and technological development.
events.detail: In the 1980s a new technological revolution was surging worldwide: the US announced its “Star Wars” program and Europe the “Eureka Project,” and competition in high technology grew fierce. In March 1986 four scientists, Wang Ganchang, Wang Daheng, Yang Jiaqi and Chen Fangyun, jointly submitted to the Party Central Committee their Proposal on Tracking the Development of Strategic High Technology in the World. After reading it Deng Xiaoping wrote: “This should be decided quickly, without delay.” That year the state drew up the Outline of the High-Tech Research and Development Program, known as the “863 Program” because the proposal and the instruction both date from March 1986. It singled out seven fields: biotechnology, space technology, information technology, laser technology, automation, energy technology and new materials, with marine technology added later, concentrating efforts to track world advanced levels. Driven by the program, China achieved a series of major results in high technology, such as the Dawning high-performance computers, some key technologies of the Shenzhou crewed spacecraft, super hybrid rice and human genome sequencing. In 1997 the state drew up the National Key Basic Research Development Plan, the “973 Program,” which mainly supported basic research in agriculture, energy, information, resources and environment, population and health, and materials. The two programs raised China’s capacity for scientific and technological innovation and narrowed the gap with developed countries. From 2016 they were merged into the National Key R&D Program.

events.title: Taiwan Compatriots Visit Relatives on the Mainland
events.short: In 1987 the Taiwan authorities allowed residents to visit relatives on the mainland, ending nearly four decades of isolation; economic and cultural exchanges then grew rapidly.
events.detail: After the Kuomintang retreated to Taiwan in 1949, the two sides of the Taiwan Strait long remained in military standoff and isolation. After the Message to Compatriots in Taiwan in 1979, the mainland actively promoted the cross-strait “three links” and exchanges. The Taiwan authorities at first held to the “three noes” policy of no contact, no negotiation and no compromise. As calls among Taiwan’s people to visit relatives grew louder, in 1987, under pressure from sources such as the “homesick” campaign of Taiwan’s veterans, the authorities were forced to adjust the “three noes.” In October that year they announced that Taiwan residents could visit relatives on the mainland, with registration from 2 November. In November the first Taiwan compatriots traveled to the mainland by way of Hong Kong, Tokyo and elsewhere, and many relatives separated for thirty or forty years were finally reunited. This ended nearly four decades of isolation and opened a new chapter in cross-strait exchanges. Afterward personnel exchanges, economic cooperation and cultural ties grew rapidly, more and more Taiwan compatriots visited relatives, traveled, invested and did business on the mainland, and Taiwan became an important trading partner and source of investment for the mainland. After 1990 the two sides set up the Straits Exchange Foundation and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits to hold working-level consultations. In 2008 the two sides achieved full, direct, two-way “three links” of mail, transport and trade. Wider exchanges deepened mutual understanding and kinship and promoted peaceful development of relations.

events.title: Development and Opening of Shanghai’s Pudong
events.short: In April 1990 the central government decided to develop and open Shanghai’s Pudong, which rapidly rose into a modern new district and drove growth across the Yangtze basin.
events.detail: Pudong lies on the east bank of the Huangpu River in Shanghai. Before reform and opening-up, poor transport left Pudong’s economy and society far behind those of Puxi on the west bank, and locals used to say, “Better a bed in Puxi than a house in Pudong.” In the 1990s, to broaden opening and spur economic growth along the Yangtze, Deng Xiaoping repeatedly urged the development of Pudong. In April 1990 the Party Central Committee and State Council formally announced the development and opening of Pudong, applying the policies of economic and technological development zones and of certain special economic zones, and it became an important window of China’s opening. The Pudong New Area successively set up national-level zones including the Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone, the Jinqiao Export Processing Zone, the Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone and the Zhangjiang High-Tech Park. The Nanpu and Yangpu bridges, the Oriental Pearl Tower and Pudong International Airport were built in turn; skyscrapers rose in Lujiazui, with the Jin Mao Tower and Shanghai Tower becoming new landmarks, and many Chinese and foreign financial institutions settled in Pudong. After Deng Xiaoping’s southern tour in 1992, development and opening picked up pace. Over more than thirty years Pudong rose from farmland and old districts into a modern new district, its gross regional product growing from about 6 billion yuan in 1990 to over 1 trillion yuan. In 2013 the China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone was inaugurated in Pudong. Pudong’s development drove growth in Shanghai and the Yangtze River Delta and became a symbol of reform and opening-up and a miniature of Shanghai’s modernization.

events.title: Deng Xiaoping’s Southern Tour
events.short: In early 1992 Deng Xiaoping toured Wuchang, Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Shanghai and gave talks answering questions that troubled people’s minds, moving reform and opening-up into a new stage.
events.detail: In the late 1980s and early 1990s the international and domestic situation changed greatly, with upheaval in Eastern Europe and the collapse of the Soviet Union; at home some people had doubts about reform and opening-up and asked whether it was “capitalist” or “socialist.” At this critical moment, from 18 January to 21 February 1992, Deng Xiaoping, then retired and 87 years old, toured Wuchang, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shanghai and other places and gave a series of important talks, known as the “Southern Tour Talks.” Deng stressed that the Party’s basic line must hold for a hundred years without wavering: “If we do not uphold socialism, carry out reform and opening-up, develop the economy and improve people’s lives, we will be left with only a dead end.” He said reform and opening-up should be bolder, with the courage to experiment: if something is judged right, try it boldly and break new ground. The criterion for judging it is chiefly whether it is conducive to developing the productive forces of socialist society, to increasing the overall strength of the socialist state and to raising people’s living standards (the “three favorables”). He also gave a penetrating account of planning and the market: “Whether there is more planning or more market is not the essential difference between socialism and capitalism. A planned economy is not equivalent to socialism, for capitalism also has planning; a market economy is not equivalent to capitalism, for socialism also has markets.” The talks theoretically answered many major questions that had long troubled and constrained people’s thinking and marked the maturing of Deng Xiaoping Theory. After the tour, a new wave of reform, opening-up and economic construction swept the country.

events.title: Establishing the Socialist Market Economy
events.short: In 1992 the 14th Party Congress set the goal of economic reform as a socialist market economy, and in 1993 the Third Plenum of the 14th Central Committee outlined its basic framework.
events.detail: Since reform and opening-up began, China’s economic reform had moved from a “planned economy supplemented by market regulation” to a “planned commodity economy.” Deng Xiaoping’s Southern Tour Talks removed the ideological constraint of treating the planned and market economies as questions of basic social system. In October 1992 the 14th National Congress of the Communist Party of China set the goal of economic reform as establishing a socialist market economy, with the market playing a basic role in allocating resources under state macroeconomic regulation. In March 1993 the first session of the Eighth National People’s Congress passed a constitutional amendment writing “the state practices a socialist market economy” into the Constitution. In November 1993 the Third Plenary Session of the 14th Central Committee adopted the Decision on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of a Socialist Market Economy, outlining its basic framework, including a modern enterprise system, a unified and open market system, a macroeconomic regulation system and a social security system. In 1997 the 15th Congress stated that public ownership as the mainstay with diverse forms of ownership developing together is the basic economic system of the primary stage of socialism. By the end of the 20th century the socialist market economy had been initially established. In 2013 the Third Plenary Session of the 18th Central Committee called for the market to play the decisive role in allocating resources while the government plays its role better. Establishing the socialist market economy was a major breakthrough in China’s economic reform, greatly freeing and developing productive forces and driving sustained, rapid economic growth.

events.title: The “1992 Consensus” and the Wang–Koo Talks
events.short: In 1992 the two cross-strait bodies each stated orally that “both sides of the Taiwan Strait adhere to the one-China principle,” the “1992 Consensus”; the Wang–Koo Talks were held in 1993.
events.detail: As cross-strait exchanges grew closer, Taiwan set up the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) in 1990 to handle practical issues arising from contacts, and the mainland set up the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) the next year. In October 1992 ARATS and SEF met in Hong Kong to discuss how to state the one-China principle in their working-level talks. In November, after an exchange of letters and messages, the two bodies reached a consensus that each would state orally that “both sides of the Taiwan Strait adhere to the one-China principle,” known as the “1992 Consensus.” Its core is that the two sides belong to one China and work together toward national reunification. It is the political foundation of cross-strait relations and laid the basis for negotiations. In April 1993 ARATS president Wang Daohan and SEF chairman Koo Chen-fu met in Singapore, the first public talks between high-level cross-strait figures, in a non-governmental capacity, since 1949, known as the “Wang–Koo Talks.” They signed four agreements including the Wang–Koo Talks Joint Agreement. The talks marked an important historic step in cross-strait relations. Later, after Taiwan’s leader put forward separatist ideas such as the “two-state theory,” talks between the two bodies were for a time suspended. After 2008 the two bodies resumed talks on the basis of the 1992 Consensus and signed more than twenty agreements, including the Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement. In 2015 the leaders of the two sides met in Singapore. Upholding the 1992 Consensus and opposing “Taiwan independence” is the key to maintaining peace and stability across the Strait and promoting its peaceful development.

images.caption: The Wang–Koo Talks

events.title: Hong Kong’s Return to China
events.short: On 1 July 1997 China resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was established, ending over 150 years of British colonial rule.
events.detail: After the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration, the Chinese government actively prepared for Hong Kong’s return. In 1990 the National People’s Congress adopted the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, setting out in law the policies of “one country, two systems,” “Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong” and a high degree of autonomy. In 1996 the Selection Committee for the first government of the Hong Kong SAR chose Tung Chee-hwa as its first Chief Executive. From late on 30 June to the early hours of 1 July 1997, the Chinese and British governments held a grand handover ceremony in the new wing of the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. At midnight on 1 July the flag of the People’s Republic of China and the flag of the Hong Kong SAR rose slowly. President Jiang Zemin solemnly declared that the government of the People’s Republic of China had resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was formally established. The return washed away a century of national humiliation, ended more than 150 years of British colonial rule and marked a great victory for the “one country, two systems” concept. After the return, Hong Kong kept its capitalist system and way of life unchanged for fifty years and continued as a free port and an international financial, trade and shipping center. The central government firmly supports the SAR government in governing according to law. In 2020 the NPC Standing Committee passed the Law of the Hong Kong SAR on Safeguarding National Security, which it said safeguards Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability. Macao also returned to China on 20 December 1999. Hong Kong’s return was an important milestone on the road to the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Jiang Zemin’s inscription: “Hong Kong will be better tomorrow”
Chinese People’s Liberation Army troops take over Hong Kong’s defense

events.title: 15th Party Congress and Deng Xiaoping Theory
events.short: In 1997 the 15th Party Congress established Deng Xiaoping Theory as the Party’s guiding ideology and set out the basic program for the primary stage of socialism.
events.detail: Deng Xiaoping died in Beijing in February 1997. He was the chief architect of China’s socialist reform, opening-up and modernization. Deng Xiaoping Theory took shape under the conditions of peace and development as the themes of the age, and answered basic questions such as what socialism is and how to build it. In September 1997 the 15th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. Jiang Zemin delivered a report titled “Hold High the Great Banner of Deng Xiaoping Theory for an All-Round Advancement of the Cause of Building Socialism with Chinese Characteristics into the 21st Century.” The Congress established Deng Xiaoping Theory as the Party’s guiding ideology and wrote it into the Party constitution. It set out the Party’s basic program for the primary stage of socialism, held that public ownership as the mainstay with diverse forms of ownership developing together is the basic economic system of that stage, and put forward the basic strategy of governing the country by law and building a socialist country under the rule of law. It also set cross-century goals: to double GNP by 2010 compared with 2000, to develop the national economy further by the Party’s centenary, and to basically achieve modernization by the centenary of the People’s Republic. In 1999 the second session of the Ninth National People’s Congress passed a constitutional amendment writing the guiding role of Deng Xiaoping Theory and the strategy of governing by law into the Constitution. Held at the turn of the century, the Congress charted the course for socialism with Chinese characteristics as it entered the new century.

sources.title: Wikipedia (Chinese) - 15th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party

events.title: Macao’s Return to China
events.short: On 20 December 1999 China resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Macao and the Macao Special Administrative Region was established, a successful application of “one country, two systems.”
events.detail: Macao has been Chinese territory since ancient times. In 1553 the Portuguese obtained the right to reside in Macao, and after the Opium War they gradually occupied it. When China and Portugal established diplomatic relations in 1979, the two sides confirmed that Macao was Chinese territory under Portuguese administration, and that the question would be settled by negotiation at an appropriate time. In April 1987 the two governments signed a joint declaration on the question of Macao, announcing that China would resume the exercise of sovereignty over Macao on 20 December 1999 and, under “one country, two systems,” establish the Macao Special Administrative Region with “Macao people ruling Macao” and a high degree of autonomy, with Macao’s existing social and economic systems and way of life unchanged for fifty years. In 1993 the National People’s Congress adopted the Basic Law of the Macao Special Administrative Region. In May 1999 Edmund Ho was elected the first Chief Executive. From late on 19 December to the early hours of 20 December 1999, the Chinese and Portuguese governments held a handover ceremony in Macao; the flag of the People’s Republic of China and the flag of the Macao SAR rose slowly, and President Jiang Zemin announced that China had resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Macao and that the Macao SAR was formally established. The song “Song of the Seven Sons: Macao,” with its line “Do you know that ‘Macau’ is not my true name,” voiced the feelings of Macao’s people about returning to the motherland. After the return, Macao’s economy grew quickly and society remained harmonious and stable. The returns of Hong Kong and Macao were an important step in washing away a century of national humiliation and achieving complete national reunification.

events.title: Western Development Strategy
events.short: In 1999 the central government announced the Western Development strategy to speed growth in the west; major projects such as the West–East Gas Pipeline and Qinghai–Tibet Railway followed.
events.detail: Since reform and opening-up began, China’s eastern coast developed first, and the gap between east and west gradually widened. The western region comprises 12 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities, including Chongqing, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Tibet, Shaanxi, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia and Guangxi, covering about 71 percent of the country’s land; it is rich in resources but relatively backward in economic and social development. As early as the 1980s Deng Xiaoping put forward the “two overall situations” concept: the coastal areas should open up faster and develop first, and the interior should take that overall situation into account; when development reached a certain point, the coast should devote more strength to helping the interior develop, which was also an overall situation. In 1999 the Party Central Committee proposed the Western Development strategy, and in 2000 the State Council set up a leading group for it, formally launching the effort. It focused on infrastructure and ecological protection: the state increased investment and policy support, built major projects such as the West–East Gas Pipeline, West–East Power Transmission and the Qinghai–Tibet Railway, and carried out ecological programs such as returning farmland to forest, returning grazing land to grassland and natural forest protection. After more than twenty years, transport, communications, energy and other infrastructure in the west improved markedly, growth quickened, living standards rose significantly and ethnic unity was strengthened. In 2020 the Central Committee and State Council issued opinions on forming a new pattern for Western Development.

events.title: China Joins the World Trade Organization
events.short: In December 2001, after 15 years of difficult negotiations, China formally joined the World Trade Organization, opening a new stage of opening-up; it later became the world’s largest goods trader.
events.detail: The predecessor of the World Trade Organization (WTO) was the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), founded in 1947, of which China was a founding contracting party. In 1950 the Taiwan authorities announced their withdrawal from GATT. In 1986 China formally applied to resume its status as a GATT contracting party, beginning long negotiations on “resuming” membership. After the WTO was founded in 1995, these became negotiations on “accession.” China insisted on joining as a developing country and on a balance of rights and obligations, and held hard bilateral talks with the US, the EU and other major members, reaching a bilateral agreement with the US in 1999 and with the EU in 2000. In November 2001 the WTO’s Fourth Ministerial Conference in Doha, Qatar, approved China’s accession, and on 11 December 2001 China formally became the WTO’s 143rd member, ending fifteen years of negotiations. After accession China kept its commitments, sharply cut tariffs and gradually opened service sectors such as banking, insurance, telecommunications and retail. Membership integrated China more deeply into economic globalization; foreign trade and foreign investment grew rapidly, and in 2013 China became the world’s largest trader in goods. China’s growth also contributed significantly to the world economy. Joining the WTO marked a new stage in China’s opening-up and was an event of historic significance in the course of reform and opening-up.
