events.title: 16th Party Congress and the “Three Represents”
events.short: In 2002 the 16th Party Congress made the “Three Represents” the Party’s guiding ideology and set the goal of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects.
events.detail: In 2000, while inspecting Guangdong, Jiang Zemin first set out the requirements of the “Three Represents” in fairly complete form: that the Party always represent the development requirements of China’s advanced productive forces, the orientation of its advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people. The thought arose from the great practice of building socialism with Chinese characteristics and answered the questions of what kind of party to build and how to build it. In November 2002 the 16th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. Jiang Zemin delivered a report titled “Build a Well-Off Society in an All-Round Way and Create a New Situation in Building Socialism with Chinese Characteristics.” The Congress established the “Three Represents,” together with Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought and Deng Xiaoping Theory, as the guiding ideology the Party must uphold over the long term, and wrote it into the Party constitution. It noted that people’s living standards had reached a moderately prosperous level overall, but one that was low, uneven and very unbalanced, and called for concentrating efforts in the first two decades of the 21st century on building a higher-level moderately prosperous society benefiting well over a billion people. The Congress elected a new central leadership with Hu Jintao as general secretary. As the first national congress of the new century, it charted the course for building a moderately prosperous society.

sources.title: Wikipedia (Chinese) - 16th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party

events.title: Shenzhou 5 and the First Chinese Spacewalk
events.short: In 2003 Yang Liwei flew on Shenzhou 5, making China the third country to master crewed spaceflight independently; in 2008 Zhai Zhigang made China’s first spacewalk.
events.detail: In the 1990s China began its crewed spaceflight program. In 1992 the central government approved the project and set a “three-step” development strategy. In November 1999 the uncrewed Shenzhou 1 spacecraft successfully completed the program’s first test flight, beginning China’s journey into space. On 15 October 2003 astronaut Yang Liwei lifted off from Jiuquan aboard the crewed Shenzhou 5 spacecraft; after about 21 hours in space and 14 orbits of the Earth, he returned safely the next day to the landing site at Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia. China became the third country after the Soviet Union and the United States to master crewed spaceflight independently, realizing the Chinese nation’s age-old dream of flight. In 2005 Fei Junlong and Nie Haisheng flew Shenzhou 6, completing a multi-person, multi-day mission. In September 2008 Zhai Zhigang, Liu Boming and Jing Haipeng flew into space aboard Shenzhou 7; Zhai left the spacecraft and waved the five-starred red flag in space, completing China’s first spacewalk. Afterward the Tiangong-1 target vehicle successfully docked with Shenzhou spacecraft, in 2013 Wang Yaping gave a lesson from space, and in 2022 the Chinese space station was completed. The achievements of the crewed space program reflect China’s scientific strength and overall national power, and gave rise to a spaceflight spirit of being “especially able to endure hardship, fight, tackle difficulties and contribute.” China’s Chang’e lunar exploration program also made great strides, and in 2019 Chang’e 4 made the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon.

images.caption: Shenzhou 5 lands successfully and Yang Liwei steps out of the capsule
Shenzhou 7: Zhai Zhigang’s spacewalk

events.title: Lien Chan’s “Journey of Peace” and Hu–Lien Meeting
events.short: In 2005 Kuomintang chairman Lien Chan led a delegation to the mainland and held the first KMT–CPC leaders’ talks in sixty years with Hu Jintao, issuing a common vision for peaceful development.
events.detail: On the basis of opposing “Taiwan independence” and upholding the one-China principle, cross-strait relations went through many twists and kept making progress. After the Democratic Progressive Party took power in 2000, the Taiwan authorities pursued a “Taiwan independence” separatist line, and cross-strait relations grew tense. In March 2005 the third session of the Tenth National People’s Congress passed the Anti-Secession Law, stating in legal form its firm will to oppose and curb separatist forces of “Taiwan independence” and safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. From 26 April to 3 May 2005 Lien Chan, chairman of the Kuomintang, led a “Journey of Peace” delegation to the mainland, paying respects at the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum and giving a speech at Peking University. On 29 April CPC General Secretary Hu Jintao held talks with Lien in Beijing, the first formal talks between top KMT and CPC leaders in sixty years, known as the “Hu–Lien meeting.” Afterward the two sides issued the Common Vision for Cross-Strait Peaceful Development. In May People First Party chairman James Soong also led a delegation to the mainland and met Hu Jintao. Lien’s trip opened a new phase in exchanges between cross-strait parties, broke the deadlock in relations and pushed them toward peace and stability. The mainland then announced measures benefiting Taiwan, including the gift of a pair of giant pandas, Tuan Tuan and Yuan Yuan, opening mainland residents’ tourism to Taiwan and wider access for Taiwan fruit. In 2008 cross-strait relations took a major turn: the two bodies resumed talks, full direct “three links” were achieved, and relations entered a new stage of peaceful development.

images.caption: Hu Jintao meets Lien Chan

events.title: Qinghai–Tibet Railway Opens
events.short: On 1 July 2006 the entire Qinghai–Tibet Railway opened to traffic, the world’s highest and longest plateau railway, ending Tibet’s lack of rail service.
events.detail: The Qinghai–Tibet Railway runs from Xining, Qinghai, in the north to Lhasa, Tibet, in the south, 1,956 km in all. The 814 km Xining–Golmud section opened in 1984, and construction of the 1,142 km Golmud–Lhasa section began in June 2001. The latter crosses the Kunlun and Tanggula mountains and other plateau terrain; it is the highest plateau railway in the world and the longest on permafrost, with more than 960 km of track above 4,000 meters. Building it meant facing “three great problems”: permafrost, extreme cold with thin air, and a fragile ecology. Builders used technical measures such as bridges in place of embankments, crushed-rock ventilated roadbeds and thermosyphon pipes to solve the worldwide problem of permafrost, and built dedicated wildlife passages to let Tibetan antelope and other animals migrate. After five years of work by over a hundred thousand builders in the “forbidden zone for life,” the whole line opened on 1 July 2006. The Fenghuoshan Tunnel, at 4,905 meters, is the world’s highest permafrost tunnel, and Tanggula Station, at 5,068 meters, is the world’s highest railway station. The railway ended Tibet’s lack of rail service, greatly strengthened links between the interior and the frontier, boosted economic and social development and tourism in Qinghai and Tibet, and promoted ethnic unity. The song “Sky Road,” with its line “That is a magical road in the sky, carrying the warmth of the world to the frontier,” expressed the joy of people of all ethnic groups. The Lhasa–Shigatse railway opened in 2014, and in 2021 the Lhasa–Nyingchi railway began operating, bringing Fuxing bullet trains to Tibet.

images.caption: Qinghai–Tibet Railway
Qinghai–Tibet Railway

events.title: 17th Party Congress and Scientific Outlook
events.short: In 2007 the 17th Party Congress wrote the Scientific Outlook on Development into the Party constitution, stressing development first, putting people first, and comprehensive, sustainable growth.
events.detail: In the 21st century China’s economy grew rapidly but also faced uneven development, mounting resource and environmental pressure, and widening urban–rural and regional gaps. In 2003 the Third Plenary Session of the 16th Central Committee proposed “putting people first and establishing a comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable approach to development that promotes the all-round development of the economy, society and people,” which became the Scientific Outlook on Development. In October 2007 the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. Hu Jintao delivered a report titled “Hold High the Great Banner of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics and Strive for New Victories in Building a Moderately Prosperous Society in All Respects.” It stated that the Outlook’s first priority is development, its core is putting people first, its basic requirement is comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development, and its fundamental method is overall consideration. The Congress wrote it into the Party constitution and set tasks such as building a harmonious socialist society and an ecological civilization. It also first put forward the concept of the “system of theories of socialism with Chinese characteristics.” Under the Outlook the state took major steps: in 2006 it abolished the agricultural tax entirely, ending the “imperial grain tax” of over two thousand years; it advanced the building of a new socialist countryside; and it introduced free compulsory education in both urban and rural areas. In 2008 China met the Wenchuan earthquake and the international financial crisis and hosted the Beijing Olympics. In 2010 its GDP passed Japan’s, making it the world’s second-largest economy. The Outlook was written into the Constitution in 2018.

images.caption: The 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China

events.title: Beijing Olympic Games
events.short: In August 2008 Beijing hosted the 29th Olympic Games, where the Chinese delegation won 51 gold medals and topped the gold-medal table for the first time, fulfilling a century-old Olympic dream.
events.detail: After the founding of the People’s Republic, China promoted sports and achieved brilliant results. In 1959 Rong Guotuan won China’s first world championship, and in 1984 Xu Haifeng won China’s first Olympic gold medal at the Los Angeles Games. In 1993 Beijing first bid for the 2000 Games and lost by two votes. On 13 July 2001 the International Olympic Committee voted in Moscow to award the 29th Summer Olympics in 2008 to Beijing, and the whole country rejoiced. The Beijing Games took “One World, One Dream” as their theme and the ideas of a “Green Olympics, High-Tech Olympics and People’s Olympics,” building venues such as the National Stadium (the “Bird’s Nest”) and the National Aquatics Center (the “Water Cube”). The opening ceremony was held at the Bird’s Nest at 8 p.m. on 8 August 2008, where the former gymnast Li Ning lit the main cauldron. In competition from 8 to 24 August, the Chinese delegation won 51 gold medals and 100 medals in all, topping the gold-medal table for the first time. The Beijing Paralympics were held successfully that September. The Games fulfilled the Chinese nation’s century-old Olympic dream, showed the world China’s achievements since reform and opening-up and the appeal of Chinese culture, and deepened mutual understanding between the Chinese people and the peoples of the world. In 2022 Beijing also successfully hosted the 24th Winter Olympics, becoming the first “dual Olympic city” to host both Summer and Winter Games.

events.title: Cross-Strait “Three Links” Achieved
events.short: On 15 December 2008 direct cross-strait sea and air transport and direct mail were fully launched, essentially achieving full, direct, two-way “three links.”
events.detail: In 1979 the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress issued the Message to Compatriots in Taiwan, first proposing the “three links” of mail, transport and trade across the Strait. For a long time afterward, because of restrictions by the Taiwan authorities, cross-strait travel and trade could only be routed through third places such as Hong Kong. As exchanges grew, the “three links” made gradual progress: in 2001 the “mini three links” opened between Kinmen and Matsu and the Fujian coast; from 2003 there were Spring Festival charter flights, later extended to other holidays. In 2008 Taiwan’s political situation changed greatly and cross-strait relations saw a historic turn. In June, after a break of nearly ten years, ARATS and SEF resumed talks in Beijing and signed agreements on weekend charter flights and mainland residents’ tourism to Taiwan. In November ARATS president Chen Yunlin led a delegation to Taiwan, held talks with SEF chairman Chiang Pin-kung and signed four agreements on sea transport, air transport, postal services and food safety. On 15 December 2008 direct sea and air links and direct mail formally began, and the two sides essentially achieved full, direct, two-way “three links,” a day regarded as a milestone in the history of cross-strait relations. The links made travel far easier for people on both sides and closed their economic ties. The two sides afterward signed a series of agreements including the Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement, and the mainland became Taiwan’s largest trading partner. As people on both sides belong to the Chinese nation, the “three links” advanced the peaceful development of relations and the well-being of compatriots on both sides.

events.title: Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway Opens
events.short: On 30 June 2011 the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway opened, about 1,318 km long, then the longest and highest-standard high-speed line ever built in a single phase.
events.detail: Before the founding of the People’s Republic, China’s transport was very backward, with only a little over 20,000 km of railway. Afterward the state invested heavily in improving transport, with great results, and after reform and opening-up the railways were sped up several times. In August 2008 the Beijing–Tianjin Intercity Railway, China’s first high-speed line designed for 350 km/h, opened. Construction of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway began in April 2008 and, after about three years, it opened on 30 June 2011. It runs from Beijing South Station to Shanghai Hongqiao Station, about 1,318 km, through seven provincial-level regions, linking the two most economically developed areas, the Bohai Rim and the Yangtze River Delta. Designed for 350 km/h, it brought the fastest Beijing–Shanghai journey to a little over four hours. Its builders overcame technical problems such as soft-soil foundations and very long bridges; the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge, 164 km long, is among the longest bridges in the world. China’s high-speed rail then grew by leaps and bounds, with the Beijing–Guangzhou, Harbin–Dalian and Shanghai–Kunming lines opening in turn and the “eight vertical and eight horizontal” network taking shape. In 2017 the Fuxing bullet trains, with fully independent intellectual property rights, first entered service on the Beijing–Shanghai line. By the end of 2023 China’s high-speed rail network exceeded 45,000 km in operation, the longest in the world. Chinese high-speed rail has become a brilliant “national calling card” and has gone abroad, taking part in overseas projects such as Indonesia’s Jakarta–Bandung high-speed railway.

images.caption: A Fuxing China Standard EMU train in service

events.title: Aircraft Carrier Liaoning Enters Service
events.short: In September 2012 China’s first aircraft carrier, the Liaoning, was handed over to the navy and J-15 fighters landed on it that year, bringing the navy into the carrier age.
events.detail: From the 1990s China’s naval weaponry was continually renewed and its level of modernization rose markedly. An aircraft carrier is a large surface warship whose main weapon is its carrier-based aircraft, and is regarded as a symbol of a country’s overall strength and naval power. The Liaoning began as the Soviet-built carrier Varyag, which was unfinished when the Soviet Union collapsed. Ukraine later sold it, a Chinese company bought it in 1998, and it was towed to Dalian in 2002. Chinese researchers and workers completed and refitted it, overcoming many technical problems. In August 2011 the carrier began sea trials. On 25 September 2012 China’s first aircraft carrier was formally handed over to the navy and named the Liaoning, hull number 16. In November that year J-15 carrier-based fighters took off and landed on the Liaoning successfully. Luo Yang, the on-site chief commander of the J-15 program, died of a sudden heart attack after the tests succeeded and has been hailed as a model of “serving the country through aviation.” The Liaoning is used mainly for research trials and training, building experience and training personnel for China’s carrier program. Carrier building then moved quickly: in December 2019 the Shandong, China’s first domestically built carrier, entered service, and in June 2022 the Fujian, its first carrier with electromagnetic catapults, was launched. The entry of carriers into service marked a new stage in naval development and is of great importance for safeguarding national sovereignty, security and development interests and world peace.

images.caption: The Liaoning

events.title: 18th Party Congress and Mo Yan’s Nobel Prize
events.short: In 2012 the 18th Party Congress elected a leadership with Xi Jinping as general secretary; the same year Mo Yan became the first Chinese citizen to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
events.detail: In November 2012 the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. It established the Scientific Outlook on Development as the guiding ideology the Party must uphold over the long term, set the goal of completing a moderately prosperous society in all respects by 2020, and laid out the overall plan of “five-sphere integration” covering economic, political, cultural, social and ecological progress, raising ecological progress to a new level for the first time with the call to “build a beautiful China.” It also advocated core socialist values: prosperity, democracy, civility and harmony; freedom, equality, justice and the rule of law; patriotism, dedication, integrity and friendship. The First Plenary Session of the 18th Central Committee elected Xi Jinping general secretary of the Party Central Committee. The Party then launched a drive on conduct and against corruption, starting with the “eight-point regulations.” In October that year the Swedish Academy announced that the 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature would go to the Chinese writer Mo Yan, honoring him for “merging folk tales, history and the contemporary with hallucinatory realism.” Mo Yan (born 1955; real name Guan Moye) is from Gaomi, Shandong, and his best-known works include Red Sorghum, Big Breasts and Wide Hips, Sandalwood Death, Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out, and Frog. As the first Chinese citizen to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, he marked an important step for Chinese literature going global. In 2015 Liu Cixin’s science-fiction novel The Three-Body Problem won the Hugo Award, and contemporary Chinese literature’s international influence has kept growing.

images.author: Source: Voice of America (photo by Dongfang)

events.title: The Chinese Dream and the “Four Comprehensives”
events.short: In 2012 Xi Jinping put forward the Chinese Dream, followed by the “Four Comprehensives”; in 2015 a new development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green, open and shared growth was proposed.
events.detail: In November 2012, while visiting the exhibition The Road to Rejuvenation, Xi Jinping said: “Realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is the greatest dream of the Chinese nation in modern times.” In 2013, at the first session of the 12th National People’s Congress, he elaborated the meaning of the Chinese Dream: national prosperity, national rejuvenation and the people’s happiness. To achieve the “Two Centenary Goals,” namely completing a moderately prosperous society in all respects by the Party’s centenary and building a prosperous, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful modern socialist country by the centenary of the People’s Republic, the Party Central Committee gradually formed the “Four Comprehensives” strategy: building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, deepening reform, advancing the rule of law and strictly governing the Party. In 2013 the Third Plenary Session of the 18th Central Committee adopted a decision on comprehensively deepening reform; in 2014 the Fourth Plenary Session adopted a decision on comprehensively advancing law-based governance, and a National Constitution Day was established. In 2015 the Fifth Plenary Session proposed the new development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green, open and shared development. The state also adopted a targeted poverty alleviation approach and launched a campaign to eliminate poverty. The Chinese Dream, the “Four Comprehensives” and the new development philosophy pointed the way for China’s development in the new era.

images.caption: Venue of the first session of the 12th National People’s Congress

events.title: The Belt and Road Initiative and the AIIB
events.short: In 2013 Xi Jinping proposed building the Silk Road Economic Belt and the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road; the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank was founded in 2015.
events.detail: The ancient Silk Road was a channel for trade and cultural exchange linking Asia, Europe and Africa. In September and October 2013, during visits to Kazakhstan and Indonesia, President Xi Jinping proposed building the “Silk Road Economic Belt” and the “21st Century Maritime Silk Road,” together known as the Belt and Road Initiative. It holds to the principles of joint consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, and aims to strengthen connectivity and practical cooperation among countries along the routes for common development. To address the shortage of funds for infrastructure in Asia, China proposed setting up the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). It was formally established in December 2015 and opened in January 2016, headquartered in Beijing, with 57 founding members, later growing to more than one hundred. China also put up funds to establish the Silk Road Fund. In 2017 and 2019 China hosted two Belt and Road Forums for International Cooperation. Under the initiative, major projects such as the China–Laos Railway and the Jakarta–Bandung high-speed railway were completed or advanced, and China–Europe freight trains grew rapidly in number, linking over a hundred Chinese and European cities. By 2023 China had signed cooperation documents on the Belt and Road with more than 150 countries and over 30 international organizations. The initiative is a major step in expanding China’s opening-up and, in China’s view, a public good it offers toward building a community with a shared future for mankind; it has promoted economic development and people-to-people ties along the routes, though it has also faced concerns and challenges over debt, the environment and other matters.

images.caption: Opening ceremony of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank
Xi Jinping declares the Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation roundtable summit open

events.title: Xi Jinping and Ma Ying-jeou Meet in Singapore
events.short: In November 2015 Xi Jinping and Ma Ying-jeou met in Singapore, the first meeting of cross-strait leaders since 1949, with both sides affirming the “1992 Consensus.”
events.detail: After 2008, on the shared political foundation of the “1992 Consensus,” cross-strait relations developed peacefully, the “three links” were achieved and more than twenty agreements were signed, including the Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement. On 7 November 2015 Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and President, met Ma Ying-jeou, the Taiwan side’s leader, at the Shangri-La Hotel in Singapore. The two met as “leaders of the two sides of the Strait” and addressed each other as “Mr.” It was the first meeting of cross-strait leaders since 1949 and a milestone in the history of cross-strait relations. In the meeting they exchanged views on further advancing peaceful development. Xi said that compatriots on both sides are one family bound by blood and that both sides should uphold the “1992 Consensus” and consolidate the common political foundation. Ma also said the “1992 Consensus” should be consolidated and the peaceful status quo maintained, and both sides affirmed the consensus’s important role. The meeting set a precedent for direct dialogue between cross-strait leaders and showed that the two sides have the ability and wisdom to solve their own problems, and the kinship of one family. Afterward Taiwan’s political situation changed: after the Democratic Progressive Party took power in 2016 it refused to recognize the “1992 Consensus,” and relations reached a stalemate. The mainland adheres to the one-China principle and the “1992 Consensus,” firmly opposes “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and interference by external forces, and has introduced measures promoting cross-strait economic and cultural exchange and giving Taiwan compatriots equal treatment, in order to advance cross-strait integration.

events.title: Defense and Military Reform: Five Theater Commands
events.short: From late 2015 China pushed defense and military reform, creating the Rocket Force and Strategic Support Force, and in 2016 replacing seven military regions with five theater commands.
events.detail: Facing the demands of the times for a strong country and strong military, China kept advancing defense and military building. In September 2015, at the parade marking the 70th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan and the World Anti-Fascist War, President Xi Jinping announced that China would cut its military personnel by 300,000. In November a Central Military Commission reform conference was held and the deepening of defense and military reform was fully launched. Reform followed the principle of “the Commission administers overall, theater commands focus on combat, services focus on building forces.” On 31 December 2015 an army leadership body, the Rocket Force (renamed from the Second Artillery Force) and the Strategic Support Force were established. In January 2016 the Central Military Commission’s organs were changed from four general departments into 15 functional departments. In February 2016 the seven military regions were reorganized into five theater commands (Eastern, Southern, Western, Northern and Central), building a new joint operational command system. In 2017 the military completed reform of its size, structure and force composition, cutting the army’s 18 group armies to 13. In July that year a parade marking the PLA’s 90th anniversary was held at Zhurihe training base in Inner Mongolia. It was the most profound and comprehensive defense and military reform since 1949, reshaping the PLA’s command system and force structure and moving it toward a world-class military. In 2024 the Strategic Support Force was disbanded and the Information Support Force and other bodies were formed.

events.title: 19th Party Congress and the New Era
events.short: In 2017 the 19th Party Congress declared that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era and made Xi Jinping Thought the Party’s guiding ideology.
events.detail: In October 2017 the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. Its theme was: “Remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind, hold high the great banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and strive to secure a decisive victory in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects.” The Congress made the major political judgment that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era, and noted that the principal contradiction in Chinese society had become the one between the people’s ever-growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. It established Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the guiding ideology the Party must uphold over the long term and wrote it into the Party constitution. It set a strategy in two stages from 2020 to the middle of this century: first, from 2020 to 2035, on the basis of a moderately prosperous society in all respects, to strive another fifteen years to basically realize socialist modernization; second, from 2035 to the middle of the century, to strive another fifteen years to build China into a prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful modern socialist country. In March 2018 the first session of the 13th National People’s Congress passed a constitutional amendment writing Xi Jinping Thought into the Constitution and establishing the National Supervisory Commission. The 19th Congress was a very important meeting held in the decisive stage of completing a moderately prosperous society, and it drew a grand blueprint for China’s development in the new era.

events.title: Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge Opens
events.short: On 23 October 2018 the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge officially opened, linking the three cities over about 55 km and forming the world’s longest sea-crossing bridge system.
events.detail: The Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge links the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in the east with Zhuhai, Guangdong, and the Macao Special Administrative Region in the west. About 55 km long in all, it is a very large cross-sea transport project combining bridges, artificial islands and a tunnel. Construction of the main works began in December 2009. They consist of roughly 22.9 km of bridges, a 6.7 km undersea tunnel and two artificial islands. The immersed tunnel is made of 33 giant sections, each weighing about 80,000 tons, joined more than 40 meters below the seabed, and is the longest immersed road tunnel in the world. The project faced a complex marine environment, difficult construction and exacting technical requirements; its builders solved a series of world-class problems, and it has a design life of 120 years. To protect the Chinese white dolphin, a Grade I nationally protected species in the Pearl River estuary, strict environmental measures were taken, so that the dolphins would stay when the bridge was built. The opening ceremony was held in Zhuhai, Guangdong, on 23 October 2018, where President Xi Jinping attended and declared the bridge open; it opened to traffic the next day. After it opened, the trip from Hong Kong to Zhuhai or Macao fell from over three hours to about forty-five minutes. It is the first very large infrastructure project jointly built by Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao under “one country, two systems,” strongly promoting the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area and strengthening ties between Hong Kong, Macao and the mainland, and reflects China’s overall strength and capacity for independent innovation.

events.title: Party Centenary and a Moderately Prosperous Societ
events.short: On 1 July 2021 a meeting marking the Party’s 100th anniversary announced that China had built a moderately prosperous society in all respects and eliminated absolute poverty for the first time.
events.detail: A “moderately prosperous society” (xiaokang) has been the ideal social condition the Chinese nation has pursued since ancient times. At the start of reform and opening-up Deng Xiaoping put forward the idea of a “moderately prosperous family,” and by the end of the 20th century people’s living standards had reached a moderately prosperous level overall. The 16th Party Congress later proposed building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, and the 18th Congress set the goal of completing it. The hardest task lay in the countryside, especially in poor areas. In 2013 Xi Jinping first proposed “targeted poverty alleviation” at Shibadong Village in Xiangxi, Hunan. The country then launched a campaign to eliminate poverty, and over 1,800 Party members and officials, including Huang Wenxiu, died on the front line. In 2020 all 98.99 million rural poor people under the current standard were lifted out of poverty and all 832 poor counties were removed from the poverty list, meeting the UN 2030 Agenda poverty-reduction target ten years early. On 1 July 2021 a grand meeting celebrating the 100th anniversary of the Communist Party was held at Tiananmen Square in Beijing, where Xi Jinping declared that, through the sustained efforts of the whole Party and people of all ethnic groups, the first centenary goal had been achieved: a moderately prosperous society had been built in all respects across China, and absolute poverty had been eliminated for the first time in history. In November the Sixth Plenary Session of the 19th Central Committee adopted the Resolution on the Major Achievements and Historical Experience of the Party over the Past Century, the third historical resolution in the Party’s history.
